docs.title: Kiestoon
docs.text:
The open source phone system for small and medium businesses. One Debian 13 machine or Proxmox container runs Asterisk 22 LTS with a modern web portal: extensions, desk phones that configure themselves, a visual IVR builder, queues, a switchboard, a user portal with drag-and-drop transfer, branch offices, high availability and more. In English and Dutch.

Install Kiestoon First setup What can it do?

docs.title: What can Kiestoon do?
docs.text:
• Telephony

    Extensions with voicemail, ring groups, call queues, conference rooms, time conditions with Dutch holidays, call recording, fax-to-mail and mail-to-fax.

    Extensions

  • Visual IVR builder

    Drag steps onto a canvas and draw lines between them. Every step has its own audio: generated from text, recorded in the browser or uploaded. Test it with one click.

    IVR builder

  • Phones that set themselves up

    Yealink, Snom, Grandstream, Fanvil, Gigaset, Poly, Htek, Akuvox and Cisco. Visual key editor, expansion modules, key templates, firmware and zero-touch provisioning.

    Phones

  • Reception and user portal

    A live switchboard and wallboard, a user portal with forwarding, voicemail, colleagues with presence and transfer by drag and drop, a browser softphone and a Windows softphone.

    User portal

  • Multi-site and high availability

    Branch offices through Kiestoon Edge (no port forwarding), linked Kiestoon systems with one phone book, and an active/passive pair that takes over when one node fails.

    Branch offices

  • Secure by default

    Mandatory MFA for admins, passkeys, SSO (Entra ID, Google, Keycloak, SAML), a managed firewall with safe mode, fail2ban, geo-blocking and outbound fraud protection.

    Security

  • Backups and updates

    Encrypted full and incremental backups to FTP, FTPS, SFTP, SCP, S3, WebDAV, SMB or OneDrive, restore from the remote location, and one-click updates on a production or testing channel.

    Backups

  • Integrations

    A REST API with tokens, signed webhooks (incoming call to your CRM), an XML and LDAP phone book, Prometheus metrics and a custom SMTP server with OAuth2 for Microsoft 365 and Google.

    API and webhooks

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Install Kiestoon on a Proxmox container or a Debian 13 machine.
  2. Follow the first setup: administrator, number plan, trunk, extensions and phones.
  3. Read how Kiestoon works for the ideas behind destinations, roles and the number plan.

Help from inside the portal

Every page in the Kiestoon portal has a Help button at the top. It opens the matching page of this manual, in the language you use the portal in.

docs.title: AI summaries
docs.text: Kiestoon can write out recorded calls and voicemail messages and summarise them: what the call was about, what was agreed, and which follow-ups somebody has to do. Open AI in the System menu.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The transcript is always made on the server by Whisper (see Speech). Audio never leaves the phone system.
  2. The summary comes from the engine you choose:
Engine What it means Local model (default) A language model runs on the server itself with llama.cpp. Free and private: nothing leaves the server. It is slower and needs free memory (about 4 GB for Qwen3 4B, 2 GB for Qwen3 1.7B). The model starts when there is work and stops after 5 idle minutes Claude (cloud) Faster and better summaries from Anthropic's Claude, with your own API key (create one at console.anthropic.com). Only the text of the transcript is sent; usage is billed by Anthropic to your account

The API key is stored apart from the other settings and is never shown again after you save it (you see only its last four characters). Remove it with Remove key.

docs.title: What to summarise
docs.text:
Setting What it does Recorded calls New recordings (of calls that are recorded anyway) are transcribed and summarised in the background, newest first, one at a time Voicemail Voicemail messages get a summary and follow-ups in the user portal, the Windows softphone and the voicemail e-mail Language of the summaries Same as the call, or always Dutch or English Keep summaries of calls Removes summaries and transcripts of calls after this many days. 0 keeps them as long as the recording exists

Press Try it to summarise a sample voicemail with the current settings before you save them.

docs.title: Summaries of recordings
docs.text:
Under Recordings (and My calls in the portal) a call with a summary shows its topic and the caller's mood. Click the sparkle button to open the summary, the follow-ups and the full transcript. Reception and administrators can also Transcribe and summarise a single recording right away, even when automatic summaries are off.

Speech recognition can make mistakes

A summary is only as good as the transcript. Names and numbers are worth checking against the recording. The model is told not to invent anything that is not in the transcript.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• The kiestoon-speech package (version 1.1.0 or newer has llama.cpp for the local model).
  • Speech-to-text turned on under Speech, with a Whisper model downloaded.
  • For the local model: the model downloaded on the AI page (pinned SHA-256 checksums).

docs.title: API, webhooks and metrics
docs.text: Everything the web portal does goes through the same JSON API under /api/. Other programs (a CRM, a helpdesk, scripts) use it with an API token. Webhooks tell those programs when something happens.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Create a token under Integrations › API tokens › New token. The token is shown once; Kiestoon stores only a hash of it.

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer kt_…" https://pbx.example.com/api/pbx/extensions
  • A token has a role (admin, reception or user) and never more rights than the user who created it has at that moment. A token of a disabled user stops working.
  • A read-only token can only use GET.
  • Tokens cannot reach /api/tokens, /api/webhooks, /api/users, /api/account, /api/auth, /api/system/updates or /api/backups/restore.
  • Write requests send JSON with Content-Type: application/json.
  • Errors come back as {"error": "<code>", "field": "<field>"} with a 4xx or 5xx status.

docs.title: Useful endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Role What GET /api/pbx/extensions admin All extensions GET /api/live reception Calls in progress, trunk status GET /api/reception/queues reception Queues with waiting callers and agents GET /api/cdr reception Call history (call detail records); /api/cdr/export gives CSV GET /api/phonebook user The central phone book POST /api/phonebook reception Add a contact {name, company, work, mobile, other, email, notes} POST /api/calls reception Click-to-call {extension: "201", number: "0201234567"}: the extension rings first GET /api/faxes reception Received faxes; GET /api/faxes/{id}/pdf downloads one POST /api/fax/send reception Send a fax {boxId, number, name, pdf}; pdf is the PDF in base64 (at most about 11 MB) GET /api/fax/jobs reception Outgoing faxes with their status (queued, sending, success, failed)

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
Add a webhook under Integrations › Webhooks › Add webhook and choose the events. Kiestoon sends a POST with JSON to your URL:

{
  "id": "4f1c2a…",
  "event": "call.ringing",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-15T09:30:12Z",
  "data": { "callId": "1731663012.42", "from": "0612345678", "fromName": "", "did": "0201234567", "extension": "201", "direction": "inbound" }
}
Event When Data call.ringing An incoming call rings on an extension callId, from, fromName, did, extension, direction call.answered An incoming call is answered same as call.ringing call.ended A call ended the call detail record voicemail.updated The message count of a mailbox changed mailbox, new, old fax.received A fax arrived id, box, status, pages, caller, did queue.abandoned A caller hung up while waiting in a queue queue, from, fromName, position, holdTime, callId

docs.title: Headers and signature
Phone book for phones
docs.text:
• XML phone books: /prov/phonebook/{yealink|snom|fanvil}.xml and /prov/phonebook/grandstream/phonebook.xml, behind the provisioning user name and password. Provisioned phones get the address automatically.
  • LDAP: base DN ou=phonebook,dc=kiestoon, attributes cn, sn, givenName, o, telephoneNumber, mobile, homePhone, mail. Bind as cn=<provisioning user>,ou=phonebook,dc=kiestoon with the provisioning password when "Require a password" is on. Only reachable from the networks that may use SIP.

docs.title: Prometheus metrics
docs.text:
Turn on Internet access › Prometheus metrics › Publish metrics. Kiestoon then serves GET /metrics (outside /api/) in the Prometheus text format. Prometheus sends the token as a bearer token; addresses in the "allowed without a token" list may scrape without one.

- job_name: kiestoon
  scheme: https
  authorization:
    credentials: <token>
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['pbx.example.com']
Metric What kiestoon_info{version} Always 1, with the running version kiestoon_uptime_seconds Seconds since the portal started kiestoon_asterisk_connected 1 when the portal talks to Asterisk kiestoon_active_calls, kiestoon_active_calls_by_direction{direction} Calls in progress kiestoon_calls_today Calls since midnight kiestoon_extensions, kiestoon_registered_endpoints Extensions and registered phones kiestoon_trunk_up{trunk} 1 when a trunk is registered or reachable kiestoon_queue_waiting_callers{queue}, kiestoon_queue_longest_wait_seconds{queue}, kiestoon_queue_available_agents{queue} Queue state kiestoon_queue_completed_total{queue}, kiestoon_queue_abandoned_total{queue} Queue counters since the last Asterisk restart kiestoon_fax_jobs{status} Outgoing faxes per status kiestoon_mail_queue_length Mails waiting to be sent kiestoon_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{target} Last successful backup per location

docs.title: Privacy policy of the Kiestoon app
docs.text:
Applies to the Kiestoon app for Android and iPhone, published by RHIS. Last updated: 27 November 2026.

The Kiestoon app is the mobile client of a Kiestoon phone system. That phone system is run by your employer or their IT partner (the "organisation"), not by RHIS. The app connects straight to the phone system of your organisation; RHIS does not run that phone system and cannot see your calls, contacts, call history or voicemail.

docs.title: What the app processes, and where it goes
docs.text:
Data Why Where it goes Address of the phone system and the sign-in session To connect to your phone system Stored on your phone only Microphone audio during a call To make the call Straight to the phone system of your organisation, encrypted (DTLS-SRTP). Never to RHIS. The microphone is only used during a call Push token of your phone (from Google Firebase Cloud Messaging or Apple) and the name of the phone (for example "Pixel 9") To ring the app for incoming calls when it is closed, and to show the phone under My devices To the phone system of your organisation. The push token is sealed by the RHIS push service, see below Your colleagues, phone book, call history, queues and voicemail To show them in the app Loaded from the phone system of your organisation and shown in the app. Not stored by RHIS

The phone system of your organisation keeps its own records (for example the call history). For those, your organisation is responsible; ask them for their privacy policy.

docs.title: The push service of RHIS
docs.text:
Google and Apple only deliver notifications for an app on behalf of its publisher, so the phone system of your organisation sends wake-up notifications through the push service of RHIS (push.rhis.nl):

  • It stores nothing: the push token is turned into a sealed handle that only the push service can open, and the handle is kept by the phone system of your organisation, not by RHIS.
  • It cannot read the notifications: who is calling and the voicemail summary are encrypted with a key that only the phone system and your phone know.
  • It logs no phone numbers, tokens or contents.

The notification itself is delivered by Google (Firebase Cloud Messaging) or Apple (Apple Push Notification service).

docs.title: What the app does not do
docs.text:
• No advertising, no tracking, no analytics and no crash reporting.
  • No access to the contacts, photos, location or files on your phone.
  • No selling or sharing of data with third parties.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Permission Why Microphone So the other side hears you during a call Notifications So the app can ring for incoming calls and show new voicemail Full-screen notification (Android) To show an incoming call over the lock screen, like the phone's own call screen Foreground service for phone calls and the microphone (Android) To keep a call going when you switch apps or lock the screen

docs.title: Your choices
docs.text:
• Unlink the phone under My devices in the Kiestoon portal (or ask your administrator). The phone system then forgets the push token at once.
  • Remove the app from your phone: everything the app stored on the phone is removed with it.
  • For data that the phone system of your organisation keeps, contact your organisation.

There are no Kiestoon accounts in the app: your account is made and removed by your organisation.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: All connections use HTTPS and encrypted audio. The software of the app and the push service is open source: github.com/rhisijmuiden/Kiestoon.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text: Questions about this policy: use the contact details of RHIS on the Google Play or App Store page of the app, or open an issue on GitHub. Changes to this policy are published on this page.

docs.title: Backups and restore
docs.text: Kiestoon makes encrypted backups to your own server or cloud storage, and restores them from the portal. It uses restic: everything is encrypted on the Kiestoon server before it leaves, and stored deduplicated, so daily backups take little space.

docs.title: What is in a backup
docs.text: Everything needed to rebuild the phone system: the database with all settings, extensions, routes, IVRs, users and call history, voicemail, recordings, faxes, voice prompts, certificates and the configuration in /etc/kiestoon. Downloaded speech models and phone firmware are left out, because they can be downloaded again.

docs.title: Backup locations
docs.text:
Under Backups › Add location choose the protocol:

Protocol Notes FTP Plain FTP sends the password unencrypted. The backup itself is always encrypted. FTPS FTP over TLS. Implicit TLS is usually port 990; off means explicit TLS (AUTH TLS) on port 21. SFTP Over SSH, with a password or an SSH private key (OpenSSH, without passphrase). SCP Uses the same SSH connection as SFTP. S3 Amazon S3, MinIO, Wasabi, Ceph, DigitalOcean, Scaleway, Hetzner, Cloudflare R2 or any other S3-compatible storage. The bucket must exist. WebDAV Nextcloud, ownCloud, SharePoint (NTLM) or another WebDAV server. For Nextcloud, use an app password. SMB A Windows share or a NAS (Synology, QNAP), SMB 2 or 3. OneDrive Microsoft OneDrive or OneDrive for Business, connected with a sign-in code.

Fill in the host, port, username, password and Folder, and click Test. The first test creates a new encrypted backup store on the location.

Store the encryption key

Kiestoon creates a strong Encryption key for every location. Without this key a backup cannot be restored on a new server. Open it with the key button on the location and store it in a password manager.

docs.title: OneDrive
docs.text:
1. Register an app in Microsoft Entra (App registrations) with Allow public client flows on and the delegated permissions Files.ReadWrite and offline_access.
  2. Fill in its Application (client) ID and save.
  3. Click Connect, open the Microsoft page that Kiestoon shows, sign in with the account the backups go to and enter the code.

docs.title: Full and incremental
docs.text:
• An incremental backup only reads files that changed since the previous snapshot. Fast and small.
  • A full backup reads every file again, so damaged or missed files are picked up as well.

Every snapshot is a complete picture: any snapshot can be restored on its own, full or incremental. Start a backup by hand with Full or Incremental on a location.

docs.title: Schedule and retention
docs.text:
With Automatic backups on, Kiestoon makes a backup every day at the chosen Time, and a full backup on the day under Full backup on. It runs for every location that is on.

Keep daily, Keep weekly and Keep monthly set how many snapshots stay. With 7 / 4 / 12 you can go back a week day by day, a month week by week and a year month by month.

A failed backup sends an e-mail to the alert address under Mail server. Recent backups shows every run with its type, trigger, size and result.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
1. Click Snapshots on a location.
  2. Pick the snapshot and click Restore.
  3. Type RESTORE to confirm and click Restore now.

Everything on this server is replaced with the backup. Calls are interrupted and the portal restarts. The current data is kept on the server as a safety copy.

docs.title: Restore on a new server
docs.text: After a broken server, install Kiestoon again (Install), add the same location and paste the key under Existing encryption key, click Test, and restore the newest snapshot. The new server then has the same extensions, phones and settings; provisioned phones simply connect again.

docs.title: Call journey
docs.text: Click any call in Call history (Reception menu) to see what happened to it, step by step: the number it came in on, the time condition, which option the caller chose in the IVR, how long they waited in the queue, whose phones rang and who missed it, who answered and for how long, transfers, voicemail and who hung up. It works for inbound, outbound and internal calls.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
• The summary at the top: caller and number called, the result (answered, voicemail, hung up while waiting, missed, busy, failed), the total time, the waiting time until someone answered and the talk time.
  • The flow: one box per step, in the style of the IVR builder. The lines carry how long the caller spent in the previous step. Zoom with the buttons or the mouse wheel; on a wide screen the boxes sit side by side.
  • Steps: the same journey as a list with the clock time of each step, also handy on a phone.
  • Recordings of the call, to play right there (see recordings).
Step Shows Incoming call Caller, number called, trunk and inbound route Call from an extension / Outbound route Who called, the number dialled, the route and trunk used Time condition Open, closed or holiday at that moment IVR menu Every key pressed, and every time the caller made no choice or an invalid one Queue Position in line, waiting time, each agent that was rung (answered, not answered, busy) and why the caller left the queue (answered, hung up, maximum waiting time, nobody signed in) Ring group / Extension Each phone that rang and how it ended; do not disturb and outside the schedule Talking with Who answered and the talk time Transferred Directly or after consulting, by whom and to whom (also when transferred by drag and drop) Voicemail, Forwarded to, Parked, Picked up by, Conference, Fax Where the call went Call ended Who hung up: the caller, the other party, an extension or the phone system

Employees see the journey of their own calls by clicking a call under My calls in the user portal. They only see calls they took part in, and only their own recordings.

docs.title: Older calls
docs.text: Kiestoon records journeys from version 0.6.0-rc.16 on. For older calls, and for calls whose journey was removed after the retention period, the page shows a short version built from the call record: who called, which phones rang and who answered.

docs.title: Retention and the GDPR
docs.text:
The journey holds phone numbers and names, so it is personal data. Under Call features & fraud › Call journey:

Setting Keep call journeys (days) Journeys older than this are removed every night. Default 90 days. 0 records no journeys at all (the call history itself stays)

Pick the shortest period you need, and mention it in your privacy statement.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: Asterisk reports every step of a call to the portal over the manager interface: Channel Event Logging (CEL) for channels, answers, bridges, transfers and hang-ups, dial and queue events for the phones that rang, and markers the generated dialplan adds at each step (route, time condition, IVR key, queue, ring group, voicemail). The portal stores them per call (the Asterisk linkedid) in its own database; nothing is written to log files on disk.

docs.title: Call quality
docs.text: Call quality (Telephony menu) shows how calls sound: MOS, jitter, packet loss and round trip, per call, per trunk and per phone. When a trunk or phone goes wrong, Kiestoon mails you, and you see on which side of the connection the problem is.

docs.title: Where the figures come from
docs.text:
During a call, Asterisk exchanges an RTCP report about every 5 seconds with each phone and each provider. Kiestoon reads both directions of every call leg:

  • Received by Kiestoon: the audio Kiestoon gets from the phone or provider, measured by Kiestoon itself.
  • Reported by the phone / provider: the audio Kiestoon sends, as the other side reports it arrived.

From jitter, packet loss, round trip and codec, Kiestoon estimates the MOS (mean opinion score) with the ITU E-model, on a scale of 1 to 4.5. A normal phone call scores about 4.4. The MOS of a call leg is its worst direction, and the MOS of a call is its worst leg. Nothing has to be set up: every call is measured.

MOS Rating 4.0 and up Good 3.6 to 4.0 Fair: people notice it, but can talk under 3.6 Poor: words drop out, people repeat themselves

docs.title: The page
docs.text:
• Alerts at the top: trunks and phones that are over their limit right now.
  • Average MOS, Poor calls, Weakest trunk and Active alerts for the chosen period (last 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days).
  • Live calls: the calls going on with their current MOS, jitter, loss and round trip, updated every 5 seconds. Click a call to open its call journey.
  • MOS by trunk: a line per trunk over the period; the shaded band is the poor range.
  • Phones with the weakest quality: the ten phones with the lowest MOS and where it goes wrong, for example "Loss towards the phone (Wi-Fi or local network)".
  • Trunks: per trunk the number of calls, average MOS, share of poor calls, jitter and loss in both directions (received by Kiestoon / reported by the provider), round trip and the trend.

Values over a limit are red. The Where it goes wrong column reads the direction: loss on the audio towards a phone points at the network of that phone; loss on the audio from a provider points at the provider or your internet line.

docs.title: In the call history
docs.text: The call history has a MOS column, and the call journey of a call shows a Call quality card: a short diagnosis, every leg with both directions, the round trip, and a strip with the MOS of each report interval, so you see when during the call it went wrong. The dashboard shows the MOS of the calls going on and the active alerts.

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
Under Call quality › Settings you set the limits and when you get a mail.

  • Limits: good from and poor under (MOS), and the limits for jitter, packet loss and round trip.
  • Trunk with poor quality: the average MOS of the last 15 minutes is under the poor limit, with at least 3 calls.
  • Phone with poor calls: at least 3 poor calls on one extension in the last 60 minutes.
  • Every poor call: a mail for each call under the poor limit. Busy installations get many mails.
  • Back to normal: a mail when the trunk or phone is back within its limits.
  • Mail to, the Quiet period before the same alert is mailed again, and how long measurements are kept (90 days by default). Send test mail sends an example alert.

Alerts use the mail server of Kiestoon and are written to the audit log.

docs.title: Prometheus
docs.text:
With metrics switched on, /metrics also has, over the last 15 minutes:

Metric What kiestoon_call_mos Average MOS of the call legs kiestoon_call_poor_total Calls under the poor limit kiestoon_trunk_mos{trunk} Average MOS per trunk kiestoon_trunk_jitter_ms{trunk}, kiestoon_trunk_packet_loss_percent{trunk}, kiestoon_trunk_rtt_ms{trunk} Jitter, loss and round trip per trunk kiestoon_active_call_mos_min Lowest current MOS of the calls going on kiestoon_quality_alerts_active Active call quality alerts

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Phones and providers that send no RTCP reports only get the direction Kiestoon measures itself.
  • A call that is still going on shows its figures so far.
  • The MOS is an estimate from network figures, not a recording of what people heard. It is a reliable guide to where problems are, and how bad they are.

docs.title: How Kiestoon works
docs.text: A few ideas come back on almost every page. Knowing them makes the rest of the manual quick to read.

docs.title: The parts
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  P[Desk phones<br>softphones<br>browser] -- SIP / RTP --> A[Asterisk 22 LTS]
  T[Telecom provider] -- SIP trunk --> A
  A <-- AMI --> K[Kiestoon portal<br>Go + SQLite]
  K -- generates config --> A
  K -- provisioning --> P
  H[kiestoon-helper<br>root] <-- Unix socket --> K
  H --> F[firewall, fail2ban,<br>backups, WireGuard, Caddy]
  • Asterisk 22 LTS handles the calls. You never edit its configuration: Kiestoon generates it from the database and reloads only what changed.
  • The Kiestoon portal is one program with the web interface, the REST API, provisioning for phones and the database (SQLite). It runs as an unprivileged user.
  • kiestoon-helper is a small root service with a fixed list of commands: apply the firewall, run a backup or restore, bring up WireGuard tunnels, configure Caddy. The portal asks; the helper checks everything again.
  • kiestoon-updater installs updates that you start from the portal, after a backup.

docs.title: Destinations
docs.text:
Almost everything that receives a call can send it on to a destination. The same list is used by inbound routes, IVR steps, time conditions, ring group and queue failover, and follow-the-sun rules:

Destination Goes to Extension One person; rings all their devices Voicemail Straight to someone's voicemail box Ring group A team, all at once or one by one Call queue Callers wait in line until an agent is free IVR menu "Press 1 for sales …" Time condition Open, closed or holiday, each with its own destination Conference room A meeting number Fax box Receives a fax and mails it as PDF External number Forward to a mobile or another number (costs an outgoing call) Linked system An extension on another Kiestoon (see linked systems) Follow the sun The team that is at work now, by time zone Hang up End the call

A typical main number: inbound route › time condition › IVR menu › ring group or queue, with voicemail when closed.

docs.title: The number plan
docs.text:
Internal numbers all have the same length: 3 digits by default, or 4 or 5.

Range (3 digits) Use 200-599 Extensions 600-699 Ring groups 700-799 Call queues (70 and 71-79 are also call parking) 800-899 Conference rooms * codes Voicemail and features, see feature codes 112, 911 Emergency, always allowed

Change the length under Settings › Number plan. Existing extensions are renumbered and provisioned phones pick up their new number by themselves.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role May Super admin Everything, including managing other super admins Administrator Manage the phone system. Always signs in with MFA Reception Switchboard, wallboard, call history, recordings and fax; sign agents in and out; switch day/night mode User Their own phone in the user portal: forwarding, voicemail, colleagues, call history, keys

A user (of any role) who is linked to an extension also gets the My workspace menu: the user portal. See Users, roles and sign-in.

docs.title: Live state
docs.text: The portal keeps a connection to Asterisk (AMI). Dashboards, the switchboard, the wallboard, colleague presence and queue status update every few seconds. Feature codes on a phone (for example *76 for do not disturb) report back to the portal, so the portal and the phone always show the same state.

docs.title: Production and testing
docs.text: Every release is first published on the testing channel as a release candidate (v0.6.0-rc.12), then promoted to production (v0.6.0). Each installation follows one channel and can switch in Info & updates. See Updates and channels.

docs.title: Conference rooms
docs.text: A conference room is a number that several people dial at the same time, from inside or outside (route a phone number to it). Numbers are in the 800 range by default.

docs.title: Create a conference room
docs.text:
1. Open Conference rooms and click New conference room.
  2. Set a PIN (empty: anyone who reaches the number can join) and a host PIN. The host PIN gives host rights: mute participants and lock the room.
  3. Maximum participants (default 20).
  4. Wait for the host: participants hear music until someone joins with the host PIN.
  5. Record meetings: the whole meeting is recorded and shows up under Recordings.

To let outside callers join, add an inbound route with the conference room as destination, or a key in an IVR menu.

docs.title: CRM integrations and call pop-up
docs.text: Kiestoon links to HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive and Exact Online. While the phone rings, a pop-up shows who is calling according to the CRM, and every call is written back to the customer in the CRM automatically. Nothing changes for installations without a CRM.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Recognising callers. As soon as a call from outside comes in, Kiestoon looks the number up in the CRMs in the order you set. Numbers are compared on their last 9 digits, so 06…, +316… and 00316… all match the same contact. Results are kept for 10 minutes.
  • Pop-up. In the web portal (on every page), the Windows softphone and the switchboard. It shows the contact, the company, open deals and tickets, the last contact and the owner, with a button to open the record in the CRM. When the browser phone rings, it also has Answer and Decline. An unknown number gets a button to create the contact.
  • Name on desk phones. The caller name on the phone display becomes Jan de Vries - Bakkerij De Vries. The call waits at most 1.5 seconds for the CRM; when it is slower the phone rings with the number only.
  • Logging calls. Every call with a customer becomes an activity on the contact (and company), under the colleague who took or made it: direction, duration, outcome and the number called. Missed calls can become a Call back task.
  • After the call the pop-up asks for a note, the outcome and an optional follow-up task. The note is added to the activity that was logged automatically.
  • Recordings never leave the server. The CRM gets a link that needs a Kiestoon login. With AI summaries of calls switched on (AI), the summary is added to the activity a few minutes later.

Only the caller's phone number goes to the CRM to look it up. Tokens and secrets are stored on the server and never shown again.

docs.title: Connecting a CRM
docs.text: Open System › Integrations › CRM and click Connect on the CRM.

docs.title: HubSpot
docs.text:
1. In HubSpot: Settings › Integrations › Private apps › Create a private app.
  2. Scopes: crm.objects.contacts.read and .write, crm.objects.companies.read, crm.objects.deals.read, tickets, crm.objects.owners.read.
  3. Paste the access token in Kiestoon and save. Kiestoon checks the token at once.

docs.title: Salesforce
docs.text:
1. In Setup: External Client App Manager › New. Enable OAuth with the scope Manage user data via APIs (api).
  2. Turn on the client credentials flow and pick a run as user that may read contacts and accounts and create tasks.
  3. Fill in your My Domain URL (https://acme.my.salesforce.com), the consumer key and the consumer secret.

docs.title: Pipedrive
docs.text:
1. In Pipedrive: your name › Personal preferences › API, copy the token. Use an account that sees all persons.
  2. Fill in the company domain (the part before .pipedrive.com) and the token.

Pipedrive organisations have no phone field, so Kiestoon looks up persons only.

docs.title: Exact Online
docs.text:
1. In the Exact App Center: Manage apps › Register a test or production app. Use the redirect URI that Kiestoon shows in the form (https://<your PBX>/api/crm/exact/callback).
  2. Fill in the country, the client ID and the client secret, then click Sign in with Exact and sign in with an Exact user that may see relations.
  3. Kiestoon refreshes the sign-in itself. Exact has no phone search, so Kiestoon keeps a list of the phone numbers of all contacts and accounts and refreshes it every hour.

Exact has no call activity: calls are logged as a communication note on the relation.

The PBX address

The redirect URI and the links to recordings use the PBX address from Separate host names or Internet access. Set it before you register the Exact app.

docs.title: Settings per CRM
docs.text: Setting What Look up contacts / companies Which records are searched for the caller's number Show in the pop-up Open deals, open tickets, last activity, owner, lifecycle stage Log every call automatically Inbound and outbound, only inbound, or only answered calls Missed calls become a task A Call back task for the owner of the contact Add a link to the recording When the call was recorded Add the AI summary When AI summaries of calls are on Create a contact for unknown numbers Off by default: colleagues create one from the pop-up Users ↔ owners Matched on e-mail address; pick an owner by hand where it differs

docs.title: For all CRMs
docs.text:
• Look-up order: the first connected CRM that knows the number wins. Unknown numbers fall back to the phone book.
  • Show the CRM name on desk phones (on by default).
  • Pop-up for everyone whose phone rings: also for colleagues in a queue or ring group. Off: only the colleague who answers sees it.

docs.title: Sync log and call history
docs.text:
The CRM sync log lists the look-ups and writes of the last 30 days. When a CRM cannot be reached, Kiestoon tries again after 1, 5 and 30 minutes and then every hour, for 24 hours; then the admins get a mail and you can Retry now. When a CRM refuses the stored sign-in, its card says Sign in again and look-ups skip it.

The call history gets a CRM column: Logged, Task created, Retrying or Not a customer. Click it to open the record in the CRM.

To test a number without calling, use Test a number on the CRM tab.

docs.title: Other software
docs.text: For a CRM that is not in the list, use the API and webhooks: the call.ringing webhook for a pop-up in your own software and POST /api/calls for click-to-call.

docs.title: Branch offices (Edge)
docs.text:
Kiestoon Edge is a small satellite for a branch office. It connects the office to the central Kiestoon (for example in a data centre) through a WireGuard tunnel and runs a SIP proxy (Kamailio) and media relay (rtpengine) for the phones in the office.

Office phones ──LAN── Kiestoon Edge ══ WireGuard (UDP 51820) ══ Kiestoon (data centre)
  SIP 5060, RTP         Kamailio, rtpengine,                       Asterisk, portal,
  provisioning :80      provisioning proxy                         all settings

Only the central Kiestoon needs a reachable UDP port. The edge connects out, so the office needs no port forwarding and NAT problems between the office and the data centre are gone: only the tunnel crosses the NAT. Extensions, voicemail and all settings stay on the central Kiestoon.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Pick one:

Where What to download from the release Raspberry Pi 3, 4, 5 or Zero 2 W kiestoon-edge-<version>-raspberry-pi-arm64.img.xz (Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit with Kiestoon Edge) Proxmox kiestoon-edge-<version>-debian-13-amd64.tar.zst (LXC template) Any Debian 13 machine kiestoon-edge_<version>_amd64.deb or _arm64.deb: apt install ./kiestoon-edge_*.deb

Raspberry Pi: write the image with Raspberry Pi Imager (Use custom). The Imager settings (user, SSH, Wi-Fi, host name) work as usual. A wired connection is recommended for phones.

Proxmox in one command: run bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhisijmuiden/Kiestoon/testing/proxmox/kiestoon-lxc.sh)" -- --edge in the shell of the Proxmox host. It downloads the Edge template and creates the container (512 MB RAM, 4 GB disk). See Installation.

LXC: the WireGuard module must be available in the host kernel (Proxmox has it). Unprivileged containers work. Without the kernel module, apt install wireguard-go makes wg-quick use the (slower) userspace implementation.

docs.title: Pair
docs.text:
1. On the central Kiestoon, open Sites → Branch offices, switch on Accept branch offices and linked systems and enter the public address of the Kiestoon. Forward UDP port 51820 to it if it is behind a router.
  2. Click Add branch office. Kiestoon shows a pairing code (valid 24 hours, works once).
  3. Open the page of the edge in the office: http://<edge address>/ and paste the code.
  4. Without a screen: put the code in a file kiestoon-edge.txt on the boot partition of the SD card (the bootfs drive on your computer). The edge reads it on start, pairs and deletes the file.
  5. On the command line: kiestoon-edge pair <code>.

The code holds the address of the portal and the SHA-256 fingerprint of its certificate. The edge only talks to a portal with exactly that certificate, so a self-signed certificate is safe. The edge generates its own WireGuard key; the private key never leaves the edge.

docs.title: Phones
docs.text:
Point the phones in the office at the edge:

  • SIP server / registrar: <edge address>, port 5060 (UDP or TCP)
  • Provisioning URL: http://<edge address>/prov/ (for example in DHCP option 66)

The edge forwards provisioning to the central Kiestoon, which hands out the edge as SIP server. Phones register through the edge (the edge adds a Path header); the central Asterisk sends calls back through the same edge. Media flows phone → edge → tunnel → Asterisk; rtpengine anchors it on both sides.

docs.title: Status and maintenance
docs.text:
• The page of the edge shows the tunnel, the last contact and the services. The central portal shows every edge with its office network, version and services.
  • The edge sends a heartbeat every 30 seconds through the tunnel. It picks up a new office address (DHCP) by itself.
  • Update the edge like any Debian package (apt install ./kiestoon-edge_<new>.deb).
  • To move an edge to another Kiestoon: kiestoon-edge reset on the edge, then pair again. Creating a new pairing code in the portal disconnects the old edge.
  • kiestoon-edge status prints the state as JSON. Logs: journalctl -u kiestoon-edge -u kamailio -u rtpengine-daemon.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Pairing from the local page is only possible while the edge is not paired, so nobody in the office can move a working edge to another system. Resetting needs a shell on the edge.
  • The edge relays requests from the office to the central Kiestoon only, with flood protection (Kamailio pike). All phones of an office share the tunnel address of the edge, so fail2ban on the central system bans the whole office when one phone keeps failing to sign in.
  • The edge holds no extension passwords; authentication happens on the central Asterisk.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Where What UDP 51820 central Kiestoon, from the internet WireGuard (changeable) UDP/TCP 5060 edge, office network SIP for the phones UDP 30000–39999 edge, office network RTP (media) TCP 80 edge, office network status page and provisioning

docs.title: Extension groups
docs.text:
An extension group is a set of extensions that call out and work the same way, for example Sales or Support. One group can do three things for all its members at once:

  • send its own number on outside calls, and get its own outbound route (for example its own trunk),
  • enforce settings such as voicemail, recording and outbound class,
  • keep the keys of their phones the same with a key template.

Open Extensions › Extension groups.

docs.title: Make a group
docs.text:
1. Click New group and give it a name.
  2. Pick an outbound caller ID (the numbers of your trunks are suggested), or leave it empty.
  3. Click the members. An extension is in one group at a time; choosing one that is in another group moves it.
  4. Tick the settings for all members you want to enforce (see below) and pick key templates if you like.
  5. Click Save. Kiestoon rebuilds the phone configuration and sends the keys to the members' phones.

You can also put a single extension in a group from its own form, with Extension group.

docs.title: Which number goes out
docs.text:
On an outside call Kiestoon sends the first of these that is filled in:

  1. the extension's own outbound caller ID,
  2. the group's caller ID,
  3. the outbound route's caller ID,
  4. the trunk's caller ID.

So a group number is the default for everyone in the group, and one person (a manager with a direct number) can still have their own. The extension form says which number it sends when its own field is empty.

docs.title: Own outbound route per group
docs.text:
Under Trunks › Outbound routes, Who can use this route limits a route to one or more groups. Members of those groups use it; everyone else skips it and takes the next route that matches. Put the group route above the general route.

Example: Support line only for the group Support, over its own trunk, above National and mobile for everyone.

A group that a route is limited to cannot be deleted; take it out of the route first. When no route is left for a caller, the call ends with a "no service" message.

docs.title: Settings for all members
docs.text:
Tick a setting to enforce it on every member. Settings you leave unticked stay per extension.

Setting Voicemail, Send voicemail to e-mail, Delete after sending Voicemail to e-mail only works for members with an e-mail address Ring time (seconds), Devices at the same time Outbound calls, Allow premium-rate numbers Recording Never, on request or always Pickup group Browser softphone

An enforced setting is locked in the extension form, with the group and the value next to it:

When you take an extension out of the group (or delete the group), it keeps the values it has; you can change them again per extension.

docs.title: Phone keys for the whole group
docs.text: Pick a key template per phone model. When you save the group, every phone of a member of that model gets the template's keys and is asked to fetch them. A phone that is linked to a member later, or an extension that joins the group later, gets them too. Send the keys to the phones again on the row repeats it, for example after you changed the template.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text: An extension is an internal number for one person or one phone, with a SIP account, a voicemail box and personal settings. Every desk phone, softphone and browser tab of that person rings on it.

docs.title: Add an extension
docs.text:
1. Open Extensions and click Add extension. Kiestoon fills in the next free number from the number plan.
  2. Fill in the name and the e-mail address.
  3. Keep Create a portal account and send a welcome e-mail on. The employee receives (in English or Dutch):
    • a one-time link to set a password (valid for 72 hours; no password is ever sent by e-mail),
    • the portal addresses, their username and extension,
    • the SIP details for a mobile softphone app, and how voicemail works,
    • a note when single sign-on is enabled.
  4. Click Save. The SIP password is generated (24 characters) and the phone configuration is rebuilt.

Without a mail server the account is still created and you get the set-password link to hand over yourself. You can send the welcome e-mail again later with the Send welcome e-mail button on the row.

docs.title: Settings per extension
docs.text: Setting What it does Transport UDP (default), TCP or TLS. With TLS you can also encrypt audio (SRTP) Devices at the same time How many devices may register at once, for example desk phone, softphone and mobile app (default 3) Extension group The extension group it belongs to. Settings the group enforces are locked in the form Outbound caller ID The number others see. Empty: the group's number, else the outbound route or trunk decides Ring time Seconds before the call goes to voicemail or the no-answer forward (default 25) Voicemail On or off, with a PIN (4-8 digits, generated when empty) Send voicemail to e-mail The message arrives as audio attachment; optionally delete after sending Outbound calls Internal only, national or international Allow premium-rate numbers 0900, 0906 and similar. Off is safer Recording Never, on request (*1 during a call) or always. See recordings Pickup group *8 picks up calls ringing in the same group Browser softphone The user can call with a headset in the user portal

docs.title: SIP details and phones
docs.text:
The SIP details button on a row shows the SIP details (server, port, username, password, voicemail number) for a softphone or a phone you set up by hand. New password makes a new SIP password; phones with the old one stop working until they get the new one. Provisioned phones get it automatically.

The Phones of this extension button on a row shows the desk phones linked to this extension, and lets you link a waiting phone right there. See Phones and provisioning.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: The Status column shows Online when at least one device is registered. The dashboard shows the same information as "Phones online".

docs.title: Forwarding, do not disturb and follow-me
docs.text: These are personal settings. The employee sets them in the user portal (My phone) or with feature codes on the phone: *72<number> forwards everything, *73 stops, *76 toggles do not disturb. Administrators see and can change the same settings in the extension form.

docs.title: Delete an extension
docs.text: The bin button deletes the extension and its voicemail box. Linked phones keep working without an account until you link them to another extension.

docs.title: Fax
docs.text: Kiestoon receives faxes and mails them as PDF (fax-to-mail), and sends PDFs as fax from the portal or by e-mail (mail-to-fax). No fax machine needed.

docs.title: Receive faxes
docs.text:
1. Open Fax › Fax boxes and click Add fax box.
  2. Fill in the e-mail addresses that get the faxes (up to 10, separated by commas), how long to keep them (0: until you delete them) and leave Error correction (ECM) on.
  3. Add an inbound route for your fax number with the fax box as destination.
  4. Switch on T.38 fax on the trunk when your provider supports it: it is more reliable than fax over G.711.

Each received fax is converted to PDF and mailed. The Received tab lists all faxes with sender, number, pages and status; download the PDF from there.

docs.title: Send faxes from the portal
docs.text:
1. On the fax box, switch on Allow sending from this box and fill in the fax number (shown to the receiver and in the fax header).
  2. Users with access open Fax › Send, choose the box, the fax number and a PDF (max 11 MB) and click Send fax.
  3. Kiestoon converts the PDF, dials, and tries again up to three times when the line is busy. At most two faxes are sent at once. The sender gets an e-mail with the result.

docs.title: Mail-to-fax
docs.text:
1. Use a separate mailbox, for example fax@yourcompany.com.
  2. On Fax › E-mail to fax, fill in its IMAP server and sign in. Kiestoon checks it every minute.
  3. Add the allowed e-mail senders to a fax box that may send, and optionally a PIN in the subject.
  4. Send an e-mail with the fax number in the subject (or to fax+0201234567@yourcompany.com when your mail server supports plus addresses) and one or more PDFs attached.

Safety

Mail that fails the SPF or DMARC check of your mail server is ignored, so a forged sender cannot send faxes. Sending depends on T.38 support of your SIP provider.

docs.title: Feature codes
docs.text:
Dial these codes on any phone or softphone. They work the same on every brand, and the portal shows the result right away (for example the do-not-disturb state). The list is also on the Call features & fraud page.

Code What it does *97 Listen to your voicemail *98 Listen to any mailbox (asks for the number and PIN) *43 Echo test: hear yourself back, to check audio *72<number> Forward all calls to a number *73 Stop forwarding *74<number> Forwarding to a number on or off (what a forward key does) *76 Do not disturb on or off *45 Sign in or out of all your queues *45<queue> Sign in or out of one queue, for example *45700 *8 Pick up a call ringing in your pickup group **<extension> Pick up a call ringing at that extension, for example **203 70 Park the current call (transfer it to 70); you hear the parking slot 71 … 79 Pick up a parked call from that slot *80<extension> Intercom: the other phone answers on the speaker *33<extension> Supervisors: listen to the queue call of that extension *34<extension> Supervisors: whisper to the agent (only the agent hears you) *35<extension> Supervisors: barge in on the queue call *1 Start or stop recording during a call (when recording is "on request") *28<id> Switch a time condition between day and night (the id is shown on the time condition) *2 Attended transfer during a call ## Blind transfer during a call 112, 911 Emergency, always allowed

Parking needs the 7 range

Call parking uses 70 and 71-79. That is why queues start at 700 in the 3-digit plan, and a linked system can not use the prefix 7.

Intercom (*80 or an intercom key) only reaches known extensions that are free and not on do not disturb. How a phone answers (automatically, with a warning tone, muted, or also during a call) is set per phone, see Phone keys and modules.

docs.title: Firewall and fraud protection
docs.text: A phone system on the internet is attacked within minutes: bots try SIP passwords day and night, and a hacked extension can call expensive numbers abroad. Kiestoon protects you in layers: a firewall, automatic blocking, geo-blocking and fraud protection on outbound calls.

docs.title: Firewall
docs.text:
Kiestoon manages an nftables firewall on the server.

Setting What it does Firewall on Blocks everything except the portal, SIP and audio ports. SIP open for everyone For phones that connect from anywhere. Not recommended: use the whitelist or Edge instead. Allow SIP from local networks Phones in the office network can always register. SIP whitelist IP addresses or networks allowed to use SIP, one per line. The addresses of your trunks are added automatically. Portal access Networks that may open the portal. Empty: everyone.

Show the generated rules shows the exact nftables rules.

Safe mode

Every change is applied in safe mode: Kiestoon checks that you can still reach the portal, and undoes the change automatically within 90 seconds if you cannot. Kiestoon also warns before you save a portal access list without your own IP address.

docs.title: fail2ban
docs.text:
With fail2ban on, an address that fails to sign in too often on SIP or the portal is blocked.

  • Attempts, Within (minutes) and Block for (minutes) set how strict it is.
  • Never block: trusted addresses, such as your office IP.
  • Blocked addresses shows the current blocks; Unblock lifts one.

docs.title: Trusted networks (skip MFA)
docs.text:
People who sign in with their password from a known network, such as the office LAN or the company VPN, can skip the MFA step there. Outside those networks the code is asked as usual.

  1. Open Firewall and scroll to Trusted networks.
  2. Add each network as an IP range in CIDR notation (192.168.1.0/24, 10.8.0.0/16, fd00:1::/64) with a description. A single address (203.0.113.10) is stored as /32 or /128. Add my address fills in the address the portal sees for you right now.
  3. Choose the roles that may skip MFA. Leave Super admin off (the default), so super admins always use their code.
  4. Switch on Skip MFA on trusted networks and click Save. This is saved straight away; it does not change the firewall rules and needs no Apply.

How it is kept safe:

  • Off by default. Every skipped MFA step is written to the audit log as login.mfa_skipped, with the network and its description.
  • Only where you are. A session that skipped MFA keeps that only while it is used from a trusted network. Take the laptop home and the portal asks for the code before you can continue (audit: session.mfa_required). Taking a role or network off has the same effect on running sessions.
  • The real address. Kiestoon uses the address of the connection. X-Forwarded-For is only believed from Caddy on this machine (internet access) or from the trusted proxies of your own reverse proxy, so a browser cannot claim to be in the office.
  • No internet-wide ranges. Ranges wider than /8, such as 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, are refused. A public range is allowed (an office with a fixed IP address) but the page warns about it: never add a range of a provider, a mobile network or a cloud.
  • Password sign-in only. Single sign-on leaves MFA to the identity provider, API tokens never ask for MFA, and passkeys already are a second factor. Administrators who have not set up MFA yet still have to do so, so it works when they are away from the office.

A trusted network is as safe as its weakest device

Anyone on that network only needs a password. Use it for networks you control, keep guest Wi-Fi out of the range, and use strong passwords.

docs.title: Geo-blocking
docs.text:
Only let telephony (SIP), and if you want the portal, in from certain countries.

  • Only allow these countries, for example with + Netherlands & Belgium or + Europe, or Block these countries.
  • Also for the web portal: port 80 stays open for Let's Encrypt.
  • Phones on your own network, the trunk providers and the whitelists always get in.
  • Colleagues who travel abroad cannot reach the phone system from countries outside the allow list.

The country data is the free "IP to Country Lite" database of DB-IP (CC BY 4.0). Kiestoon downloads it once a month; Update country data fetches it right away.

docs.title: Fraud protection
docs.text:
Under Call features & fraud › Toll-fraud protection you limit what can be dialled, and Kiestoon raises the alarm on unusual traffic, so a stolen password does not cost a fortune.

Setting What it does Premium-rate prefixes Blocked for extensions without Allow premium-rate numbers, such as 0900 and 0906. Blocked country codes Never dialable, for example 7, 234 or 882. Maximum simultaneous outbound calls A hard limit for the whole system. 0 is unlimited. Alert above outbound calls / Alert above international calls Per hour. 0 turns the alert off. Alert email Who gets the alarm. Empty: the notification address under Mail server. Block all outbound calls on an alert Stops all outbound calls until an administrator clicks Unblock. Emergency calls stay possible.

Per extension, Outbound calls sets what it may dial: Internal only, National or International.

Emergency calls always work

112 and 911 work from every extension, without a route, during a fraud block and even when a trunk limit is reached. See Settings.

docs.title: The same page: parking and recording
docs.text:
• Call parking: dial 70 to park a call; it goes to slot 71 and up. A parked call that nobody picks up rings back at the person who parked it.
  • Recording: how long recordings are kept (mind the GDPR), and an optional beep every 15 seconds so callers know they are being recorded.

docs.title: First setup
docs.text: This guide takes a fresh Kiestoon from the first sign-in to the first real phone call. Plan about half an hour. Each step links to the full chapter.

docs.title: 1. Sign in for the first time
docs.text:
Open the URL from the installer or the console (http://<server>:8080) and sign in with the user name admin and the generated password (shown again with sudo kiestoon initial-admin). The portal then asks for:

  • Language. Every user picks their own language later.
  • Organization name: shown in the portal and later on phone displays.
  • Your name and your own password (at least 12 characters; a sentence of a few words works well). The generated password stops working.

Administrators always use two-factor authentication. Right after choosing your password, scan the QR code with an authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator, 1Password …), enter the 6-digit code and save the recovery codes. Each recovery code works once, if you lose your phone.

Joining as a standby node

The first screen also has Join an existing Kiestoon as standby node. Use that only for the second machine of a high-availability pair.

docs.title: 2. Basic settings
docs.text:
Open Settings (bottom of the left menu).

  1. Number plan: internal numbers have 3 digits by default (extensions 200-599, ring groups 600-699, queues 700-799, conference rooms 800-899). Click Change number length for 4 or 5 digits; existing extensions are renumbered for you.
  2. Calls: language of the prompts (English or Dutch, also used for voicemail e-mails), time zone and country code (31 for the Netherlands).
  3. Emergency calls: 112 and 911 always work from every extension. Set the caller ID for emergency calls to a number that can be called back and is tied to your address.
  4. Network and NAT: when the server is behind NAT and phones connect from outside, fill in the public address and the local networks.

See Settings for every option.

docs.title: 3. Mail server
docs.text: Voicemail to e-mail, welcome e-mails, fax and alerts need a mail server. Open Mail server, fill in your SMTP server (or sign in with Microsoft 365 / Google OAuth2) and send a test mail. See Mail server.

docs.title: 4. Connect your telecom provider
docs.text:
Open Trunks & routes:

  1. Trunks › Add trunk: pick your provider template (for example Voys or Cheapconnect) and fill in the account details. The status turns Registered.
  2. Inbound routes: send each phone number somewhere: an extension, a ring group, a queue, an IVR menu or a time condition.
  3. Outbound routes: add a route with the Dutch numbers preset and choose the trunk(s).

See Trunks and Inbound and outbound routes.

docs.title: 5. Add extensions
docs.text: Open Extensions › Add extension. Kiestoon picks the next free number and generates a strong SIP password. Fill in the e-mail address and keep Create a portal account and send a welcome e-mail on: the employee gets a link to set a password, the portal address and the details for a softphone app. See Extensions.

docs.title: 6. Connect phones
docs.text:
Open Phones & provisioning:

  1. Turn provisioning on and copy the provisioning URL.
  2. Put that URL in DHCP option 66 of your router, or enter it in the phone's web interface.
  3. Plug in the phones. They show up under Waiting for an extension: pick an extension and click Link.

See Phones and provisioning and Phone keys and modules.

docs.title: 7. Secure and back up
docs.text:
• Switch on the firewall with the SIP allow list of your provider and fail2ban. Safe mode rolls back a change if you lose access. See Firewall.
  • Add a backup location (SFTP, FTPS, S3, OneDrive …) and a schedule, and write down the encryption key. See Backups.
  • Check Info & updates (bottom of the left menu) for the channel and the latest version. See Updates.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Administrator with MFA and saved recovery codes
  • Number plan, time zone, prompt language, emergency caller ID
  • Mail server tested
  • Trunk registered, inbound and outbound route
  • Extensions with welcome e-mails
  • Phones linked and calling
  • Firewall on, backups scheduled, encryption key stored safely

docs.title: High availability
docs.text: Two Kiestoon systems can run as an active/passive pair. The primary node runs the phone system; the standby node copies its database and files continuously and takes over when the primary fails.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
1. Install Kiestoon twice, with the same version (two LXC containers on different Proxmox hosts, or two machines).
  2. On the first system (finish its first sign-in): Sites → High availability, choose the failover mode and click Switch on high availability. Kiestoon shows a join code.
  3. Open the portal of the second system. Sign in with the user name and password of the second system, choose Join an existing Kiestoon as standby node and paste the code.

The second system restarts as standby. Its portal shows the replication state and a Promote form; everything else is managed on the primary.

docs.title: Failover modes
docs.text:
Virtual IP (same network). Both nodes are in one network (layer 2). keepalived (VRRP, unicast between the nodes) holds a virtual IP on the primary; phones and trunks use that address. When the primary fails, the standby takes the virtual IP within a few seconds and promotes itself. Both nodes run keepalived in BACKUP mode with nopreempt, so a recovered node does not take the address back by itself.

By hand or by DNS. The nodes are in different networks or data centres. Promote the standby from its own portal (sign in with an administrator account of the primary) and point DNS (for example SRV records with a short TTL) or the phones at it.

docs.title: What is replicated
docs.text:
• The database: the primary takes a consistent snapshot (VACUUM INTO) within seconds of every change; the standby fetches it through the tunnel.
  • Files: the Asterisk spool (voicemail, recordings), prompts, fax, speech models, firmware and TLS certificates, compared by size and checksum every few seconds.
  • Generated configuration (Asterisk, firewall, provisioning) is not copied: it is rebuilt from the database.

All replication runs through a dedicated WireGuard tunnel (kt-ha, UDP 51821) with a shared secret, so it also works across the internet.

docs.title: Switch over
docs.text: Switch over on the primary hands over cleanly: it takes a last snapshot, waits until the standby has it, then steps down. The standby promotes itself; the old primary becomes the new standby. Use this for maintenance and updates: update the standby, switch over, update the old primary.

docs.title: Split brain and data loss
docs.text:
• Calls in progress are dropped when the other node takes over. Registrations come back within the re-register interval of the phones.
  • Changes of the last few seconds before a crash can be lost.
  • When the standby is promoted while the primary still runs (network split), both nodes can run the phone system. The manual promotion refuses this while the primary still answers, unless force is checked.
  • Virtual IP mode: when the nodes see each other again, keepalived keeps one master and the other node steps down to standby and copies from the master. Changes made on the node that stepped down during the split are lost.
  • By hand or by DNS: an old primary that comes back still thinks it is the primary. Keep it off the network (or stop kiestoon and asterisk on it), then reinstall it and join it as the new standby.
  • A node that is promoted keeps its own previous database in /var/lib/kiestoon/cluster/previous, for recovery by hand.

docs.title: Switch off
docs.text: Switch off on the primary removes the pair. The standby hears it, forgets the pairing and becomes an empty system again (setup wizard).

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Between the nodes What UDP 51821 both ways WireGuard tunnel for replication TCP 8443 standby → primary, once joining VRRP (protocol 112) both ways, virtual IP mode only keepalived

docs.title: Call history
docs.text:
Call history (Reception menu) lists every call: time, caller, called number, direction, result, duration and trunk. Search on a number, filter on date range, direction (inbound, outbound, internal) and result (answered, no answer, busy, failed), and click Export CSV for a spreadsheet. Click a call to see its call journey: every step it went through, drawn as a flow.

Employees see their own calls in the user portal under My calls, with click-to-call to call someone back.

docs.title: Recordings
docs.text:
Calls are recorded when:

  • an extension has recording Always on,
  • an extension has recording On request and the user presses *1 during the call (again to stop),
  • a queue has Record queue calls on,
  • a conference room has Record meetings on.

Recordings (Reception menu) lists them with date, from, to and length. Listen in the browser, download or delete. Employees find their own recordings in the user portal.

docs.title: Retention and the GDPR
docs.text:
Under Call features & fraud › Recording:

Setting Keep recordings (days) Older recordings are removed automatically. 0 keeps them forever; mind the GDPR (AVG) retention rules Beep during recordings Callers hear a short beep every 15 seconds

Tell callers you record

Under the GDPR you must tell callers that calls may be recorded and why. A line in the welcome prompt of your IVR menu or queue is the usual way.

docs.title: Separate host names
docs.text:
Kiestoon can use two addresses on the same server:

Address Example Used for PBX address https://sip.example.com or https://voip.example.com Administration, phone provisioning, firmware, phone book, SIP registration, SAML Employee portal address https://voipcentrale.example.com The user portal, welcome e-mails, set-password links, the Windows softphone

Both addresses reach the same Kiestoon. Without an employee portal address everybody uses the PBX address, as before.

docs.title: With the built-in internet access (Caddy)
docs.text:
1. Create DNS records for both names, pointing to your public IP address.
  2. Go to Internet access, fill in the Domain name (the PBX address, e.g. sip.example.com) and the Employee portal host name (e.g. voipcentrale.example.com), and save.
  3. Caddy gets a separate Let's Encrypt certificate for each name. The Certificate block shows both.

When Use the certificate for SIP over TLS too is on, the certificate of the PBX address is used for SIP.

docs.title: Behind your own reverse proxy
docs.text:
1. Go to Internet access › Own reverse proxy, set the Public address (PBX) and the Employee portal address.
  2. Point both host names at the same Kiestoon in your proxy. Pass the Host header unchanged (or set X-Forwarded-Host; Kiestoon only reads it from a trusted proxy).

nginx example with two server blocks:

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name sip.example.com voipcentrale.example.com;
    ssl_certificate     /etc/ssl/example.com/fullchain.pem;   # a certificate for both names
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/example.com/privkey.pem;
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://10.0.0.20:8080;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host              $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade           $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection        $connection_upgrade;
    }
}

docs.title: Blocking administration on the employee portal address
docs.text:
In the Host names block, switch on Block administration on the employee portal address. On that address:

  • administrators get the user portal and the switchboard, never the administration pages or the admin API;
  • the menu shows Administration is closed on this address with a link to the PBX address;
  • employees and reception work as usual.

You can only switch this on from the PBX address, so you cannot lock yourself out.

Keep administration off the internet completely

Kiestoon tells the addresses apart by host name. Anyone who knows the PBX address and can reach the server can still try it. For full separation, only publish the employee portal address in your proxy or public DNS, and reach the PBX address from your own network or a VPN. Combine this with Firewall rules for the admin networks.

docs.title: What goes where
docs.text:
Link or setting Address Welcome e-mail, set-password link Employee portal Pairing the Windows softphone Employee portal Browser softphone (WebRTC) The address the page was opened on SIP server shown in the portal and welcome e-mail PBX host name Phone provisioning, firmware, phone book XML, zero-touch PBX address OpenID Connect sign-in The address you signed in on (register both callbacks, shown in Host names) SAML sign-in PBX address Passkeys Per address: a passkey made on one address does not work on the other

SIP (5060/5061) and audio (RTP) never go through a web proxy: phones register directly with the PBX host name, so its DNS record must point to the address where those ports are forwarded.

docs.title: Hot desks
docs.text: A hot desk is a desk phone that anyone can use as their own: they log in with their extension number and PIN, and the phone loads their account. Calls to their extension ring there, and calls they make show their number.

docs.title: Setting up a hot desk
docs.text:
1. Create an extension for the desk, for example 290 Hot desk 1. This is the guest account the phone uses while nobody is logged in. You can give it limited outgoing rights.
  2. Go to Phones & provisioning, click Edit on the phone and choose that extension.
  3. Under Hot desk, switch on This phone is a hot desk. Switch on Log out every night if desks should be free every morning (everyone is logged out at 03:00).

Hot desking works on every provisioned desk phone. It has been built for Yealink.

docs.title: Logging in and out
docs.text:
Code What it does *55 Log in: enter your extension number and #, then your PIN and # *56 Log out: the phone goes back to its guest account

The PIN is the voicemail PIN of the extension. An extension without a PIN cannot log in.

After you log in or out, the phone reloads its settings within a few seconds. You can put *55 and *56 on a speed dial key to make it one press.

  • An extension is logged in on one hot desk at a time: logging in on another desk logs it out on the first one.
  • The keys of the phone stay the same; the account on line 1 changes.
  • Your own desk phone and the softphone keep working. If the extension allows only one device at a time (Devices at the same time 1), the hot desk takes over from the other device.
  • After 5 wrong PINs, the desk is locked for 10 minutes.

docs.title: In the admin console
docs.text: The phone list shows who is logged in on each hot desk. Click the log out icon to free a desk. Every login and logout is in the audit log.

docs.title: Import from another phone system
docs.text:
System › Import takes over the configuration of your old phone system: extensions, ring groups, queues, voice menus with their recordings, opening hours, trunks and phone numbers. You upload a backup or the configuration files, check a preview, tick what you want and Kiestoon creates it. Nothing changes in Kiestoon until you press Import.

System What you upload UniFi Talk The Talk backup (.unifi) from UniFi OS Asterisk /etc/asterisk as a .tar.gz or zip, or the loose .conf files FreePBX, Issabel, PBXact A FreePBX backup (.tar.gz or .tgz) or a mysqldump of the asterisk database FreeSWITCH and FusionPBX /etc/freeswitch as an archive, or a FusionPBX backup with its database dump 3CX A 3CX backup (.zip) without a password, or the extension list exported as CSV

docs.title: The steps
docs.text:
1. Upload. Pick the system (or leave it on Detect automatically) and drop the files. You can upload up to 50 loose files at once, or one archive of up to 2 GB.
  2. Preview. Kiestoon shows everything it found, grouped by kind, with a free number in your number plan for each item. The old number is kept when it fits your number plan. You can change every number and untick what you do not want. Voice menus are shown as a tree with their keys, and every recording can be played. Remarks about things that could not be taken over are listed under Notes.
  3. Import. The recordings are converted to telephone quality (8 kHz) in your browser and saved as prompts. Then the items are created: first the extensions, ring groups, queues, trunks and opening hours, then the voice menus and inbound routes that point at them.

When a destination was not ticked, the call hangs up at that point and the preview says so. Things that already exist in Kiestoon with the same name are reused, so you can run the import again without duplicates. The uploaded files are kept for at most two hours and are removed when you close the import.

Backups contain passwords

A backup of a phone system holds SIP passwords of phones and trunks. Kiestoon keeps a SIP password when it is strong enough, so a phone only needs the new server address. Weak passwords are replaced by a new one, which the preview shows.

docs.title: Asterisk
docs.text:
Upload the folder /etc/asterisk as a .tar.gz or zip. To bring the recordings along, add /var/lib/asterisk/sounds/custom (or wherever your recordings are) to the same archive, or upload them as loose files next to the configuration.

tar czf asterisk-config.tar.gz /etc/asterisk /var/lib/asterisk/sounds/custom

Kiestoon reads:

From Asterisk Becomes in Kiestoon pjsip.conf endpoints (also the pjsip wizard) and sip.conf peers, users.conf Extensions with their SIP password pjsip.conf registrations and endpoints with a remote host, sip.conf peers with register => Trunks voicemail.conf Voicemail on/off, PIN and e-mail per extension queues.conf Queues with their members and settings extensions.conf: Dial to several phones Ring groups extensions.conf: Background + WaitExten with keys Voice menus with their recordings extensions.conf: GotoIfTime Time conditions extensions.conf: numbers in the context of the trunk Inbound routes

Templates ([name](!)), #include files and (+) additions are followed. Dialplan steps that Kiestoon has no equivalent for (AGI scripts, database lookups, custom macros) are named in the notes. Recordings in .wav, .ulaw, .alaw, .sln and .gsm are recognised; GSM cannot be converted in the browser, so upload those again as WAV or MP3 under Prompts.

docs.title: FreePBX, Issabel, PBXact
docs.text:
In FreePBX 15, 16 or 17, go to Admin › Backup & Restore, make a backup with all modules and download the .tar.gz. Backups of FreePBX 2.x to 14 (.tgz) and of Issabel or Elastix work as well; they are read from the database dump inside. A loose mysqldump of the asterisk database also works:

mysqldump asterisk > asterisk.sql

Kiestoon reads the extensions (with voicemail settings), ring groups, queues, IVRs with their system recordings, announcements, time conditions with their time groups, misc destinations, trunks and inbound routes. Feature codes are not imported, because Kiestoon has its own (see Feature codes).

docs.title: FreeSWITCH and FusionPBX
docs.text:
For FreeSWITCH, upload /etc/freeswitch as an archive. Kiestoon reads the users and groups of the directory, the gateways, the callcenter queues, the IVR menus with their sound files and the dialplan: the public context gives the inbound numbers, conditions on wday/time-of-day become time conditions. Add the recordings folder (for example /usr/share/freeswitch/sounds/custom) to the archive to bring them along.

For FusionPBX, upload a FusionPBX backup, or a database dump next to the recordings:

pg_dump -U fusionpbx fusionpbx > fusionpbx.sql
tar czf fusionpbx.tar.gz fusionpbx.sql /var/lib/freeswitch/recordings

Both the plain (.sql) and the custom format (pg_dump -Fc) are read. Kiestoon takes the extensions, voicemail, ring groups, call center queues, IVR menus, gateways, destinations (inbound numbers) and recordings of the first domain. FusionPBX time conditions are not imported; set them up again on the Time conditions page.

docs.title: 3CX
docs.text:
In 3CX, go to Admin › Backup, make a backup without a password and download the .zip. Do not unpack and re-pack it. 3CX encrypts the configuration of a backup with a password, and only 3CX itself can read that; Kiestoon then asks for a backup without one.

3CX does not publish the layout of its backups, so Kiestoon looks for the extensions, ring groups, queues, digital receptionists, trunks and inbound rules by name, and takes the recordings from the httpprompts folder. Check the preview carefully before you import.

The extension list from Users › Export (a .csv file) can be uploaded as well, on its own or next to the backup. Since 3CX 20 that export no longer contains the SIP passwords, so the extensions get a new password.

docs.title: After the import
docs.text:
• Check the voice menus in the IVR builder and make a test call.
  • Add the phones on the Phones page; phones are not imported, because Kiestoon provisions its own.
  • Move the phone numbers to the new trunk at your provider.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Kiestoon runs on Debian 13 "Trixie" (amd64 or arm64). Pick one of two ways: the ready-made Proxmox LXC template, or the installer on a Debian 13 server or virtual machine. Both end with the same result: a running portal, and the address, user name and password to sign in with. Everything else you set up in the portal.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: Minimum Comfortable for 50+ users CPU 1 core 2 cores Memory 1 GB 2 GB (4 GB with local speech-to-text) Disk 8 GB 20 GB or more for recordings and voicemail Network A fixed IP address in the office network Plus a public host name for remote phones and the softphone

docs.title: Download from URL in Proxmox
docs.text:
Proxmox's own template list (CT Templates › Templates) only shows the official Proxmox and TurnKey appliances, and you cannot add other sources to it. Proxmox can download any template from a URL, though:

  1. In Proxmox, open your storage (for example local) › CT Templates › Download from URL.

  2. Paste this URL, click Query URL and then Download:

    https://github.com/rhisijmuiden/Kiestoon/releases/latest/download/kiestoon-debian-13-amd64.tar.zst

    Until the first stable release

    latest only points to stable releases. Until there is one, use the URL of the newest release candidate, for example https://github.com/rhisijmuiden/Kiestoon/releases/download/v0.7.0-rc.28/kiestoon-debian-13-amd64.tar.zst (on the releases page, copy the link of kiestoon-debian-13-amd64.tar.zst). Kiestoon Edge: kiestoon-edge-debian-13-amd64.tar.zst.

  3. Click Create CT. Pick the template, keep Unprivileged container and Nesting on, and start with 1 CPU, 1 GB RAM and 8 GB disk. Give it a fixed IP address (or a DHCP reservation).

  4. Start the container and open its Console. Above the login prompt it shows only what you need:

      Kiestoon portal: http://192.168.1.20:8080
  Username:        admin
  Password:        k7Rm-Xq4T-9fwP-Lh2c

  5. Open the URL, sign in, and continue in the portal.

docs.title: In one command on the Proxmox host
docs.text:
Open a shell on the Proxmox host (node › Shell) and run:

bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhisijmuiden/Kiestoon/testing/proxmox/kiestoon-lxc.sh)"

The script finds the newest release, downloads the LXC template to the template storage (local by default) and checks its SHA-256 checksum. It then shows a summary, creates an unprivileged container (1 CPU, 1 GB RAM, 8 GB disk, DHCP on vmbr0), starts it and prints the URL, user name and password.

Useful options:
