Option What it does --download-only Only put the template in CT Templates; create the container yourself --edge Use the Kiestoon Edge template instead --ip 192.168.1.20/24 --gateway 192.168.1.1 Fixed IP address instead of DHCP --id 120 --hostname pbx Container ID and host name --storage local-zfs --disk 16 Storage and size of the root disk --cores 2 --memory 2048 CPU and memory --bridge vmbr1 --vlan 20 Network bridge and VLAN tag --channel testing / --version v0.7.0-rc.26 Release channel or a fixed version --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub Put an SSH key on the container --yes Do not ask for confirmation

Pass options after --, for example:

bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhisijmuiden/Kiestoon/testing/proxmox/kiestoon-lxc.sh)" -- --ip 192.168.1.20/24 --gateway 192.168.1.1

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
1. Download kiestoon-<version>-debian-13-amd64.tar.zst from the releases on GitHub.
  2. In Proxmox, open your storage › CT Templates › Upload and upload the file.
  3. Create a container from the template. Unprivileged is fine. Start with 1 CPU, 1 GB RAM and 8 GB disk, and give it a fixed IP address (or a DHCP reservation).
  4. Start the container. The console shows the URL, user name and password.

Testing channel

Release candidates (vX.Y.Z-rc.N) come with a template too. A container made from an rc template follows the testing channel; a stable template follows production. You can switch later, see Updates.

docs.title: Option 2: Debian 13 server or VM
docs.text:
Run the installer as root on a clean Debian 13 machine:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhisijmuiden/Kiestoon/testing/install.sh | sudo bash

To follow the testing channel (release candidates):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhisijmuiden/Kiestoon/testing/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --channel testing

Until the first stable release, only the testing channel has releases, so use --channel testing for now.

Installer options:

Option What it does --channel production|testing Update channel to follow (default production) --version vX.Y.Z Install exactly this release instead of the newest --deb, --asterisk-deb, --sounds-deb, --speech-deb Install local packages (for development) --dry-run Only show which release would be installed, change nothing

The installer adds the packages kiestoon (portal and API), kiestoon-asterisk (Asterisk 22 LTS, built for Kiestoon), kiestoon-sounds-nl (Dutch voice prompts) and the services kiestoon-helper (a small root helper for the firewall, backups and tunnels) and kiestoon-updater. It works the same on hardware, in a virtual machine or in a container. At the end it prints only what you need:

Kiestoon v0.7.0 is installed.
  URL:      http://192.168.1.20:8080
  Username: admin
  Password: k7Rm-Xq4T-9fwP-Lh2c

docs.title: Open the portal
docs.text:
Address When http://<server>:8080 Always, in your own network https://<server>:8443 Same portal over HTTPS with a self-signed certificate. Needed for the browser softphone (microphone) https://<your domain> After you switch on internet access (Let's Encrypt on port 443)

The password is generated for each installation. Lost it before the first sign-in? Show it again on the server:

sudo kiestoon initial-admin

At the first sign-in you choose your own password; the generated one then stops working and is no longer shown.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Open these in a firewall in front of Kiestoon. The firewall page in the portal opens exactly these on the server itself.

Port What 8080/tcp, 8443/tcp Portal (HTTP, HTTPS) and phone provisioning (/prov/) 80/tcp, 443/tcp Only with internet access switched on (Caddy, Let's Encrypt) 5060/udp+tcp, 5061/tcp SIP, SIP over TLS 10000-20000/udp Audio (RTP) 51820/udp WireGuard for branch offices and linked systems (only when switched on) 51821/udp WireGuard between the two nodes of a high-availability pair (only when switched on) 389/tcp, 636/tcp LDAP phone book, own network only (only when switched on)

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text:
Path What /etc/kiestoon/kiestoon.env Settings: listen port, data directory, default channel /var/lib/kiestoon/ All state: database, generated Asterisk config, voicemail, recordings, faxes, mail queue /etc/asterisk/ Static Asterisk config that includes the generated files. Do not edit by hand /var/lib/kiestoon-backups/ Automatic backups made before every update (the newest 5 are kept)

One rule behind everything

All state lives in /var/lib/kiestoon, and every generated configuration (Asterisk, firewall, provisioning) can be rebuilt from the database. That keeps backups, restores and high availability simple.

Next: first setup.

docs.title: Internet access and SSL
docs.text: On your own network the portal is always at http://<server>:8080 (and https://<server>:8443 with a self-signed certificate). To reach the portal, the softphone and passkeys from anywhere with a trusted certificate, switch on Internet access. Kiestoon then starts Caddy on ports 80 and 443 and gets a free certificate from Let's Encrypt for your domain name, and renews it on its own.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. DNS: create an A record (and AAAA for IPv6) for the domain name, for example pbx.example.com, pointing to your public IP address. Kiestoon shows where the name points now, and warns when it does not resolve yet.
  2. Router: forward ports 80 and 443 (TCP) to the Kiestoon server.
  3. In Kiestoon, go to Internet access, switch on Direct internet access, fill in the Domain name and an E-mail for Let's Encrypt (it gets a message if renewing fails), and save.
  4. Caddy gets the certificate within about a minute. The Certificate box shows who it is for, the issuer and the expiry date. Without a certificate yet, Caddy tries again every few minutes.

The firewall opens ports 80 and 443 automatically.

Option What it does Use the certificate for SIP over TLS too Phones and softphones trust the encrypted SIP connection (port 5061) without installing a certificate. Test certificates (Let's Encrypt staging) For trying things out without hitting the Let's Encrypt rate limits. Browsers do not trust these certificates.

docs.title: What works over the internet address
docs.text:
• The admin portal and the user portal, with a valid padlock.
  • The browser softphone and the Windows softphone (WebRTC over secure WebSockets).
  • Passkeys, which need https and a host name.
  • Links in welcome e-mails, voicemail e-mails and zero-touch provisioning.

Already a reverse proxy?

Do you already have nginx, Traefik, HAProxy or a firewall with a web proxy in front? Leave internet access off and follow Own reverse proxy.

Telephones from outside

Internet access is for the web portal and the softphones. Desk phones and SIP apps outside the office still need SIP to be allowed in the firewall. For branch offices, use an Edge: it connects through an encrypted tunnel, without opening SIP to the internet.

A separate address for employees

Fill in Employee portal host name to give employees their own address with its own certificate, see Separate host names.

docs.title: IVR builder
docs.text: The IVR builder is your digital receptionist: "Welcome to Noordkade. For sales press 1, for support press 2." You build the menu visually: drag steps onto a canvas, connect them by drawing lines, and give every step its own audio.

docs.title: Create a menu
docs.text:
1. Open IVR builder and click New IVR menu. The canvas opens with one step: Incoming call.
  2. Click Incoming call and give the menu a name in the side panel. Set:
    • Wait for a key: seconds the menu waits after the announcement,
    • Repeat menu: how many times the menu plays again before giving up,
    • Allow dialing an extension: callers who know an extension can dial it directly,
    • Caller language: the language of this menu, when it differs from the caller language of the system. It is also the default language of text you have spoken.
  3. Give the incoming call its audio message (the welcome text), see Audio per step.
  4. Drag building blocks from the bar above the canvas (or click them to add), and connect them.
  5. Click Save, then Test call.

Blocks show live details: whether a time condition is open right now, how many agents of a queue are online and whether an extension is available. The buttons at the right of the bar switch between flowing and angular lines and turn the moving dots on the lines (the direction of the call) on or off.

docs.title: Building blocks
docs.text:
Block What it does Lines out Incoming call Start of the menu; plays the welcome message To the keypresses and No input, or one start step Choice menu A further menu with its own message and keys, for example one per branch of a time condition To its keypresses and No input Keypress "Press 1": the caller pressed this key One, or several destinations that ring together No input The caller pressed nothing or an unused key, after the menu repeated One Play audio Plays a message, then does what you chose under After the message One Speech question Asks what the caller wants and listens to the answer (see below) One per answer, plus Not understood Extension, Ring group, Queue, Voicemail Transfers the call there End point Submenu Another IVR menu End point External number Forwards to a phone number outside End point On-call Rings whoever is on duty in an on-call team right now End point Time condition Checks the opening hours and the day/night switch Two: open and closed Back to menu Back to the start of a menu: the one the caller came from, the main menu or a choice menu you pick End point Hang up Ends the call End point

Linked systems add Other site, and follow-the-sun routes can be a target too.

docs.title: Drawing lines
docs.text:
Drag from the dot on the right of a step to the next step. A keypress only belongs to the menu when a line runs from Incoming call to it. A time condition has two dots: open and closed.

The canvas helps you along:

  • Steps with a problem get a warning: Not part of the menu, No line leads to this step, No line goes out: the call ends here, Choose where the call goes.
  • Undo / Redo (also Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z), Tidy up lays the flow out neatly, the minimap and zoom buttons help with large menus.
  • Duplicate in the side panel copies a step.
  • Keyboard: press Enter on a step to select it, then move it with the arrow keys.

docs.title: Check the time first
docs.text:
Want the time to decide which menu callers get? Draw the line from Incoming call to a Time condition instead of to keys. That step then runs right after the welcome message. Draw open and closed each to a Choice menu, and give each menu its own keys and No input. A choice menu plays its own message (for example "Press 1 for support") and waits for a key, just like the start of the menu. The same key can be used in different menus.

New keys from the palette go into the selected choice menu (or the menu of the selected key). Keys that hang off Incoming call while it has a start step are skipped; the canvas warns about this.

docs.title: Copy and paste
docs.text:
Right-click a step for Copy, Copy with the steps after it, Paste, Duplicate and Delete; the same buttons are at the bottom of the side panel. Select several steps with Ctrl-click or by dragging a box with Shift, then use Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V. The clipboard stays in your browser, so you can paste into another menu too.

Where the copy goes depends on what you paste on:

  • A copied choice menu on another menu (a choice menu or Incoming call): that menu gets the same keys, no-input step and everything after them. Typical: copy the open-hours menu with its steps, right-click the empty Closed menu and choose Paste into this menu, then change what differs. A key whose digit the menu already has stays loose and is flagged.
  • Copied keys on a menu: they join that menu.
  • One copied step on a step with a free dot: it is connected after that step.
  • On the empty canvas: the copy is placed where you clicked, without lines.

docs.title: Phone numbers
docs.text: Click Incoming call to see which phone numbers ring this menu. Add a number lists the free numbers of your trunks (and numbers that go elsewhere now, which then move to this menu), or type another number. This creates the inbound route right away, the same one you see under Trunks & routes › Inbound routes; the × removes it again. The numbers show on the Incoming call step. Save a new menu once before linking numbers.

docs.title: After the message
docs.text:
When you select a Play audio step, the side panel shows After the message with a Then list:

  • The menu the caller came from, the main menu or any choice menu: the caller hears that menu again and can choose once more;
  • Hang up;
  • Go on to a step: any step already on the canvas, such as a queue or another message.

Your choice draws the line on the canvas, so you always see what happens. A new audio step goes back to the menu the caller came from until you choose something else. You can still drag the line yourself; the list follows it.

A Back to menu step does the same on its own: pick in its side panel which menu it goes back to.

docs.title: On-call after hours
docs.text: Use the On-call block for calls outside office hours, for example under a key of the closed choice menu after a time check. Pick the on-call team in the side panel. The block shows who is on duty now (and the backup); the call then follows the escalation of the team, see On-call. An on-call team can also be the overflow of a queue: choose On-call team under When the queue is full or too slow in the queue.

docs.title: Ring several destinations at once
docs.text: A keypress (or No input, Play audio, a time condition or speech answer) can ring up to five destinations at the same time: draw a second line from the same dot, for example to a queue and to an external number. The first to answer gets the call; the others stop ringing. This works for extensions, ring groups, queues and external numbers. While the phones ring, the caller hears the music of the queue (or ringing when there is no queue). When nobody answers within the maximum wait of the queue (60 seconds without a queue), the call follows the overflow of the queue.

docs.title: Queue settings in the editor
docs.text: Click a Queue step to change the queue itself in the side panel: agents, distribution, ring and wait times, greeting, music, position announcements, callback and overflow. Save queue stores it straight away, apart from the menu, and the change applies everywhere the queue is used. New queue creates a queue right there and points the step to it.

docs.title: Audio per step
docs.text:
Every step that plays something (incoming call, keypress, no input, play audio) has its own audio message, with a waveform player to listen to it. Choose the source in the side panel:

Source How Generate Type the text, choose the engine (Local (Piper) or ElevenLabs) and a voice, and click Generate audio. With a locked voice profile the voice is fixed and only the text is needed. Piper runs on the server; ElevenLabs gives studio-quality voices (see ElevenLabs voices). Needs Speech switched on Record Record with the microphone in the browser (needs https) Upload Drop an MP3, WAV, M4A or OGG file (max 10 MB). Converted to telephone quality Library Pick an existing voice prompt None No audio

Generated, recorded and uploaded audio is saved under Voice prompts, so you can reuse it in queues and other menus.

docs.title: Speech question
docs.text:
A Speech question lets callers say what they are calling about instead of pressing keys ("Please tell us in a few words what you are calling about").

  1. The step plays its question, then records the answer (up to 12 seconds; 3 seconds of silence ends it).
  2. The answer is written out on this server by Whisper, while the caller hears hold music for a moment.
  3. Every answer of the step has a name and keywords. The answer with the most keywords that occur in what the caller said wins. A keyword also matches longer words (factu matches factuur and facturen); capitals and accents do not matter, and a keyword of several words (werkt niet) must occur in that order.
  4. With Let AI choose when no keyword matches, the AI engine picks the answer that fits best. Claude takes a second or two; a local model can take much longer the first time.
  5. Nothing fits, or speech-to-text is off: the call takes the Not understood line.

Every answer has its own port on the right of the step; draw a line from each to where the call should go. A common set-up: connect No input to the speech question and set Repeat menu to 0, so callers who press nothing are asked to say it, while callers who know the key still press it. The call journey shows what the caller's answer was recognised as.

Requirements

Speech-to-text must be on under Speech with a Whisper model downloaded. The base or small model keeps the wait short.

docs.title: Test call
docs.text: Click Test call, enter your extension and click Call me. Your phone rings; answer it to hear the menu as a caller would. Save the menu first.

docs.title: Use the menu
docs.text:
An IVR menu is a destination. Use it in an inbound route, behind a time condition (open › menu, closed › voicemail), or as a submenu of another menu.

A complete main number

Inbound route 050 700 1234 › time condition Office hours › open: IVR Main menu (1 › Sales intro › ring group Sales, 2 › queue Support, 3 › Daan, no input › repeat), closed: voicemail.

Older menus

Menus made before the canvas existed (list of keys) are converted to a flow automatically the first time you open them.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: System › Logs shows what the phone system and the portal write down. Use it to find out why something does not work: a trunk that does not register, a phone that cannot sign in, a call that fails, a backup or mail that goes wrong.

docs.title: The logs
docs.text: Log What is in it Phone system Notices, warnings and errors of Asterisk (/var/log/asterisk/messages.log): trunk registrations, calls that fail, phones that cannot sign in Security Sign-in attempts on phone accounts, also failed and blocked ones (security.log). The firewall (fail2ban) reads this log Portal Messages of the Kiestoon portal: mail, backups, updates, integrations System helper The service that applies the firewall, backups, internet access and updates as root Phone engine service Start, stop and crashes of the Asterisk service

docs.title: Searching
docs.text:
• Search shows only the lines that contain all the words you type, for example a host name, a phone number, an extension or trunk-3. The words are highlighted.
  • Show limits the lines to notices and worse, warnings and errors or errors only.
  • Follow reloads the log every 5 seconds, handy while you try something on a phone.
  • Download saves the whole log as a text file, for example to send to your supplier.

The newest line is at the top. The viewer reads the end of the log (the last few megabytes, including the previous week when the log has just been rotated); for older lines use Download. The Asterisk logs are rotated weekly and kept for 8 weeks.

docs.title: Why a trunk does not work
docs.text: When a trunk is Rejected, Not registered or Unreachable, the trunk list shows the reason under the status, read from the phone system log, for example Sign-in refused (401): the user name or password is wrong. Click Show log lines for what to check and the log lines about that trunk, and Open in logs to see everything around it.

docs.title: Mail server
docs.text: Kiestoon sends e-mail for voicemail, faxes, welcome mails, fraud alerts and failed backups. It uses your own SMTP server, so the mail comes from your own domain.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
1. Go to Mail server and pick a Quick setup: Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or Other server.

  2. Check the Host, Port and Encryption:

    Encryption Port Use STARTTLS 587 Most servers, Microsoft 365 TLS 465 Gmail, many hosting providers None 25 Only an internal relay. Passwords and messages travel readable over the network.

  3. Choose how to Sign in:

    • Username and password: classic SMTP AUTH. Use an app password where the provider offers one.
    • OAuth2 · Microsoft 365: for tenants where basic authentication is switched off. Register an app in Microsoft Entra with the application permission SMTP.SendAsApp and admin consent, give it access to the mailbox in Exchange Online, and fill in the Mailbox, Tenant ID, Client ID and Client secret.
    • OAuth2 · Google Workspace: an OAuth client in Google Cloud with a Refresh token for the mailbox (scope https://mail.google.com/).
    • None: for a relay that accepts mail from this server's address.
  4. Fill in the From address and From name, for example pbx@example.com and "Kiestoon".
  5. Send alerts to: the address for failed backups, fraud alerts and other problems.
  6. Switch Sending on and save.
  7. Under Send a test, fill in a recipient and click Send test.

Do not check the certificate is only for an internal server with its own certificate.

docs.title: The mail log
docs.text: Recent e-mails shows every message with time, recipient and result. While sending is off, or when the server cannot be reached, e-mails wait in a queue and are sent as soon as it works again; the page shows how many are waiting.

docs.title: What Kiestoon e-mails
docs.text: E-mail Set up in Voicemail with the audio, and a transcription with speech-to-text Voicemail Received faxes as PDF Fax Welcome mail with a set-password link Users Fraud alerts Fraud protection Failed backups Backups

docs.title: Mobile app
docs.text:
The Kiestoon app for iPhone and Android takes an extension along on the road. It rings with the calls for the extension, also when the app is closed and the phone is locked, and shows new voicemail as a notification with the AI summary. It has the same screens as the Windows softphone: colleagues with live status, the phone book, queues, voicemail and call history.

Availability

The apps are published by RHIS as Kiestoon in the App Store (iOS 16 and later) and Google Play (Android 10 and later). Until the store release they are available as a test version (TestFlight and a Google Play test track); ask RHIS for an invitation.

docs.title: Switch it on
docs.text:
Open Mobile app in the System menu and turn on Allow the mobile app. Nothing else is needed: the phone system talks to the push service of RHIS by itself.

Setting What it does Allow the mobile app Employees can link the app under My devices. Turning it off stops all wake-up notifications; linked phones stay in the list Push service address Leave it empty for https://push.rhis.nl. Only change it when you publish your own build of the app (see Your own push service) Test connection Checks that this server reaches the push service and shows whether it delivers to iPhone, Android or both

The table Linked phones shows every phone with its employee, when the app was last used and when the last notification went out. Unlink removes a phone (for example a lost one); the app stops ringing at once. A phone whose app was removed is unlinked by itself at the next notification.

docs.title: Link the app (employees)
docs.text:
1. Install Kiestoon from the App Store or Google Play.
  2. In the portal, open My devices and press Link mobile app. A QR code appears.
  3. Scan it with the camera of the phone. The app opens, links itself to your extension and asks to allow notifications and the microphone. Allow both: without notifications the app cannot ring when it is closed.

The code works once and for 10 minutes. On a phone without a camera, open the app, choose Link with code and type the server address and the code. Linking uses the sign-in of the portal, so it works the same with a password, MFA, a passkey or single sign-on: the app itself never sees a password.

Under My devices you see your linked phones. Send test notification checks that notifications arrive; Unlink removes a phone.

docs.title: Using the app
docs.text:
The app has the screens of the Windows softphone, with the menu as a tab bar at the bottom. An incoming call shows on the phone's own call screen: on iPhone the CallKit screen (also on the lock screen and in the car), on Android a full-screen call with Answer and Decline. During a call the phone keeps the microphone and the audio running when you switch apps or lock the screen; on Android a notification shows the call in progress with Hang up.

New voicemail shows as a notification. On Android it shows the caller and the AI summary; on iPhone it reads New voicemail, open the app to see who called and the summary.

When Allow the mobile app is off, or the app was built without push (see Build the app), the app still works as a softphone while it is open, like the browser softphone.

docs.title: How a call reaches the phone
docs.text:
A phone in a pocket has no open connection to the phone system: iOS and Android close it to save the battery. So the phone system wakes the app first:

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant K as Kiestoon
    participant R as Push service (RHIS)
    participant A as Apple / Google
    participant P as Phone
    C->>K: call for 204
    K->>R: wake 204 (signed, content encrypted)
    R->>A: VoIP push / high priority message
    A->>P: wake the app
    P->>P: shows the call (CallKit / Android call screen)
    P->>K: connects and registers (WebSocket, SRTP)
    K->>P: the waiting call rings

The desk phone, the browser and the Windows softphone ring at the same moment, as always. The call waits up to 15 seconds for the phone to connect; on a normal 4G or Wi-Fi connection that takes one or two seconds. When the caller hangs up first, or a colleague answers, the call screen on the phone goes away again.

Calls through ring groups and queues reach the app the same way. Intercom calls do not: the app never answers by itself.

docs.title: Privacy and security
docs.text:
Apple and Google only deliver notifications for an app on behalf of its publisher, so a phone system cannot send them directly. The push service of RHIS forwards them and is built so that it needs as little trust as possible:

  • It stores nothing. When a phone links, the push service turns the push token of the phone into a sealed handle that only the push service can open, and forgets it. Your phone system keeps the handle.
  • It cannot read the notifications. Who is calling and the voicemail summary are encrypted with a key that only your phone system and the phone know. The push service only sees that a notification goes to a phone.
  • Every phone system has its own key (shown on the settings page). A handle only works with the key of the phone system that made it, and every request is signed and works once, so nobody else can ring your phones.
  • It logs no numbers, tokens or contents. The push service is open source (cmd/kiestoon-push in the repository).

Calls themselves never go through RHIS: the app connects straight to your phone system with encrypted audio (WebRTC, DTLS-SRTP), the same way as the Windows softphone. For calls from outside the office the portal must be reachable from the internet, see Internet access and SSL.

docs.title: Your own push service
docs.text:
Only the publisher of an app can send to it. When you build and publish the app yourself (under your own name in the stores), run your own push service with your own Apple and Google keys:

  1. Install the package kiestoon-push_<version>_amd64.deb (or arm64) from the releases on a small Debian server.
  2. Apple: create a key with Apple Push Notifications service under developer.apple.com > Keys, and copy the .p8 file to /etc/kiestoon-push/apns.p8. Google: create a service account key in the Firebase project and copy it to /etc/kiestoon-push/fcm.json. Give both chgrp kiestoon-push and chmod 0640.
  3. Fill in /etc/kiestoon-push/kiestoon-push.env (key id, team id, bundle id of your app), remove KIESTOON_PUSH_LOG_ONLY=1 and run systemctl restart kiestoon-push.
  4. Put an HTTPS proxy in front, for example Caddy: push.example.com { reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8095 }.
  5. On every phone system, enter https://push.example.com as Push service address and press Test connection.

The secret in /var/lib/kiestoon-push/secret seals the handles. Back it up: with a new secret every phone has to open the app once to register again.

docs.title: Build the app
docs.text:
The source of the app is in the folder mobile/ of the repository (Tauri 2, with a small native part in Kotlin and Swift for push and the call screen). Every change is built by GitHub Actions (workflow Mobile app): a debug APK for Android and a simulator build for iPhone. For your own store build you need:

  • Android: a Firebase project with an Android app nl.rhis.kiestoon (or your own id). Put its google-services.json in mobile/src-tauri/gen/android/app/; without it the app builds without push. Sign the release APK or bundle with your upload key. The workflow Mobile app (Google Play) does this for the RHIS release: it builds the signed App Bundle and uploads it to Google Play, see mobile/store/README.md.
  • iPhone: an Apple developer account, a Mac with Xcode, and the capabilities Push Notifications and Background Modes (Voice over IP, Audio, Remote notifications). Run npx tauri ios init and then ./ios-setup.sh in mobile/, which adds the background modes, the microphone text and the push entitlement.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution The app only rings when it is open Notifications are not allowed for Kiestoon. Turn them on in the settings of the phone, open the app once, and use Send test notification Test connection says the push service cannot be reached The server needs outgoing HTTPS to push.rhis.nl (port 443). Check the firewall between the server and the internet The call screen appears but the call does not connect The phone cannot reach the portal over the internet. Check Internet access, or connect to the office Wi-Fi A phone no longer shows in the list The app was removed or reinstalled; Apple or Google then report the phone as gone and it is unlinked. Link it again

docs.title: Linked systems
docs.text:
Two or more Kiestoon systems (for example an office in the Netherlands and one in the US) can be linked. They keep their own extensions, trunks and settings, and get:

  • one phone book: the numbers of the other site appear with a site prefix (for example 8 + 201);
  • free internal calls through an encrypted WireGuard tunnel, with the caller shown as prefix + number so call back works;
  • busy lamp (BLF) keys for colleagues on the other site (key value: prefix + number);
  • queues with agents on both sites;
  • follow the sun: a number goes to the site that is open now, each in its own time zone.

docs.title: Link two systems
docs.text:
1. On system A: Sites → Branch offices, switch on the tunnel hub and enter its public address. Forward UDP 51820 (and TCP 8443 for pairing) to it.
  2. On system A: Sites → Linked systems → Invite a system. Enter the name and prefix the numbers of B get on A.
  3. On system B: Linked systems → Join with a code. Paste the code and choose the prefix the numbers of A get on B.

B connects to the hub of A; only A needs open ports. A star works too: several systems join one hub. The code pins the certificate of A, like an edge pairing code (see Branch offices).

A prefix must not overlap with the numbers on the system (extensions, ring groups, queues, conference rooms, parking 70–79) or with another link. Prefixes start with 1–9; 0 stays the outside line.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Each link is a PJSIP endpoint fed-<id> over TCP to the tunnel address of the other system, identified by that address. Dialling <prefix><number> goes to the other system, which only routes it to its own internal numbers (never to its trunks), so a link cannot be used to make outside calls on the other side.
  • Every minute each side fetches the phone book of the other (/api/fed/v1/directory through the tunnel, with a per-link token). Changes in busy state are pushed straight away and fully every minute.
  • Busy lamps of remote numbers are custom device states (Custom:ktfed<id>-<number>), updated by the portal.
  • Remote queue agents are Local/<number>@kiestoon-fedout-<id> members with that custom device state, so the queue knows when they are in a call.
  • Dial without prefix when unique (per link): numbers of that site that do not exist locally can be dialled without the prefix.
  • Routing destinations: Linked system (a number on the other site) and Follow the sun can be chosen everywhere a destination is chosen (inbound routes, IVR, time conditions, queue overflow).

docs.title: Follow the sun
docs.text: Sites → Follow the sun: a list of rules, each with a time zone, days and hours and a destination. The first rule that matches the current time in its own time zone gets the call; otherwise the fallback destination does. Example: Amsterdam 08:00–17:00 (Europe/Amsterdam) to the Dutch support queue, New York 09:00–17:00 (America/New_York) to the American support queue on the linked system, else voicemail.

docs.title: Unlinking
docs.text: Removing a link on one side tells the other side, removes the endpoint and clears destinations that pointed to it.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Where What UDP 51820 hub, from the other systems WireGuard TCP 8443 hub, once while pairing portal (HTTPS)

docs.title: On-call
docs.text:
An on-call team is an internal number that rings the engineer who is on call at that moment, on their own mobile number. Kiestoon works out who that is from the schedule: you do not change any routing by hand when the duty changes. When the engineer does not answer, the call moves down the escalation steps: the backup, the team lead, everyone, a fixed number, and finally a destination such as a voicemail box. Numbers are in the ring group range.

Engineers see their shifts under My on-call shifts in the portal and can swap or hand over shifts with colleagues there. A swap goes around the regular schedule for that period only.

docs.title: Create an on-call team
docs.text:
1. Open On-call and click New on-call team. Give the team a name and a number.
  2. On the Schedule tab, choose how the duty rotates:
    • Weekly rotation: the engineers take turns per week. Set the hand-over day and time (for example Monday 08:00) and the start date: the first engineer in the list is on call from the hand-over on or before that date.
    • Daily rotation: the same, per day.
    • Planned shifts: no rotation; you plan every shift on the overview with Temporary override.
  3. Add the engineers in the order of the rotation. Each engineer is called on the mobile number in their own profile. A missing number shows a warning; click the number to change it.
  4. Backup (2nd line): the next engineer in the rotation, a fixed person, or nobody.
  5. Team lead: called in the team lead step, gets mails about gaps in the schedule and approves swaps.
  6. Swaps and hand-overs: approved right away once the colleague accepts, or after approval by the team lead or an administrator.
  7. Reminders: engineers get a mail the day before their shift starts.

To have a caller reach the on-call team, pick On-call team as the destination of an inbound route, a time condition (for example outside office hours) or a key in an IVR menu.

docs.title: Escalation
docs.text:
The Escalation tab lists the steps that run from top to bottom until someone answers. Per step you choose who is called and for how many seconds:

Step Who is called Engineer on duty (1st line) The engineer on call according to the schedule, swaps included Backup (2nd line) The backup at this moment Team lead The team lead of the team Everyone All engineers of the team at once A user One fixed person A number A fixed phone number, for example an external service desk

A step without anyone to call (no backup, or a gap in the schedule) is skipped. Repeat steps runs the whole list again, up to five times. After the last step the call goes to If nobody answers.

  • Engineer presses 1 to accept: the engineer hears that this is an on-call call and presses 1. A mobile voicemail that picks up can then never take the call; without the 1 the next step follows.
  • Also ring the extension and app: the engineer's own phone, softphone and Kiestoon app ring next to the mobile.
  • Music while waiting: the caller hears music on hold instead of ringing.
  • Greeting for the caller: a prompt played first, such as "You are being connected to the engineer on duty".
  • Caller ID prefix: put in front of the caller's name, so engineers see that it is an on-call call.

Every on-call call shows in the call journey: which step rang whom and who accepted.

docs.title: Temporary override
docs.text:
On the overview, Temporary override puts someone on call for a while, for example when an engineer is ill. An override beats the regular schedule and the swaps made before it. The Swaps and changes tab lists all overrides, swaps and hand-overs; you can cancel them there.

The overview also shows Attention points: gaps in the next 14 days where nobody is on call, and engineers without a mobile number. The team lead gets a mail about gaps.

docs.title: Calendar link
docs.text: Under Schedule, Calendar link (iCal) gives a link you subscribe to in Outlook, Google or Apple Calendar. Anyone with the link can read the schedule; New link stops the old one. Engineers find the same link on their own page.

docs.title: My on-call shifts
docs.text:
Engineers open My on-call shifts in the portal. They see:

  • their mobile number, which they can change themselves;
  • whether they are on call now, and their upcoming shifts;
  • the schedule of the next 14 days.

Swap next to a shift asks a colleague to take it:

  • Hand over: the colleague takes your shift (or part of it, from a time until a time).
  • Swap: the colleague takes your shift and you take one of theirs in return.

The colleague accepts or declines in their own portal and gets a mail. Depending on the team's setting, the team lead then approves. Until then the regular schedule applies. Take over now puts yourself on call right away, for example when the engineer on duty asked you by phone.

docs.title: Phone keys and modules
docs.text: Every desk phone has a visual key editor: a picture of the phone with its keys left and right of the display, in pages, plus any expansion modules. Click a key to set it up; drag a key onto another to swap them, also onto another page or module.

docs.title: Open the editor
docs.text:
• Administrators: Phones & provisioning, click Edit on a phone.
  • Employees: in the user portal under Softphone & devices they edit the keys of their own phone and modules.

docs.title: Key types
docs.text:
Type What the key does Value Line A line (account) on the phone Line number BLF (colleague) Shows whether a colleague is free, ringing or busy; press to call, or to pick up when it rings Extension Speed dial Calls a number Phone number Park call Parks the current call; the caller hears music until someone picks it up at a parking slot (71-79) Parking slot Lights up when a call is parked there; press to pick it up 71 … 79 Intercom Calls a colleague who answers on the speaker Extension Do not disturb Switches DND on and off (*76), with the lamp showing the state Voicemail Calls your voicemail (*97) Forward Forwards all your calls at once; press again to stop. The lamp is lit while you forward External number, or a destination: colleague, voicemail, ring group, queue, IVR menu, time condition, conference room, on-call team, follow the sun, fax box Empty Does nothing

Each key also has a label for the display.

docs.title: Forward key
docs.text:
A forward key switches unconditional forwarding of the phone's own extension (line 1) on and off. It uses the same forwarding as *72/*73 and the Forward all calls setting of the extension, so the portal, the app and the phone always agree.

Under Forward to an administrator chooses where the calls go: an external number, or anything inside Kiestoon, for example the on-call team or an IVR menu with the on-call message. Employees who edit their own keys in the portal can enter an external number only.

  • Press the key: all calls go to the destination of the key. The lamp lights up.
  • Press again: forwarding stops and the lamp goes out. If you were forwarding to another number (set with *72 or in the portal), the key also switches that off.
  • The phone dials *74<extension>*<number> (for a destination inside Kiestoon *74<extension>***<code>); Kiestoon adds that code to the dialplan when you save a phone with a forward key. Calls forwarded out go through the outbound routes with the rights of the extension.

Put a forward key in a key template to give every phone of that model the same key, for example a key to the on-call team. It works on all Yealink models and on every brand that has BLF keys.

docs.title: Extra lines
docs.text: Line 1 is the extension of the phone. Desk phones of Yealink, Snom and Grandstream can carry extra lines (accounts 2 and up), for example a shared sales line. Choose the extensions under Extra lines and put them on line keys.

docs.title: Expansion modules
docs.text:
Click Expansion module and choose the module. All modules on a phone are of the same type.

Module Keys For Max Yealink EXP40 40 (2 pages of 20) T46U, T48U 6 Yealink EXP43 60 (3 pages of 20) T43U, T46U, T48U 3 Yealink EXP50 60 (3 pages of 20) T53W, T54W, T57W 3 Snom D7 18 D717, D735, D785 3 Grandstream GBX20 40 (2 pages of 20) GXP2170, GRP2616 4

The Yealink T41P, T41S, T41U, T42G, T42S and T42U take no expansion module. They have 6 physical line keys; with more than 6 keys set, the sixth key switches between 3 pages of 5, so you can set up 15 keys. The T42S and T42U carry up to 12 lines, the T41 models 6 and the T42G 3.

Module keys are set up exactly like phone keys. A reception module full of BLF keys shows the whole office at a glance.

docs.title: Key templates
docs.text:
A key template is a key layout for one phone model, including its expansion modules. Use it to give all reception phones, or all phones of a team, the same keys.

  1. Set up one phone and click Save as template, or open the Key templates tab and click New template.
  2. On the template, click Apply to phones, choose the phones of that model and confirm. Their keys and modules are replaced.
  3. Phones that are online fetch their new keys right away; the others at their next provisioning check.

Load template… in the editor of a single phone copies a template onto that phone before you save it.

docs.title: Intercom
docs.text:
Intercom (*80<extension> or an intercom key) only reaches known extensions that are free and not on do not disturb. It rings all their devices, including the browser softphone. Per phone you choose how it answers:

Option Effect Answer intercom calls automatically The phone picks up on the speaker Play a warning tone first A short beep before the caller is heard Start with the microphone muted The callee is only heard after pressing mute Also during another call The intercom call is answered while the user is on the phone

The phone form only shows the options the brand supports:

Brand Options Yealink, Snom, Fanvil All four Poly Automatic answer and muted microphone Grandstream, Htek, Cisco MPP, Akuvox door stations Automatic answer on or off

docs.title: When do phones get their keys?
docs.text: After you save, Kiestoon tells a registered phone to fetch its configuration (check-sync). The keys change within a few seconds. A phone that is not registered picks the change up at its next provisioning check or after a reboot.

docs.title: Phone book
docs.text: The phone book holds shared contacts for everyone: in the portal, on the desk phones (XML), over LDAP, and for the names of incoming callers.

docs.title: Contacts
docs.text:
• Add contact: name, company, work, mobile and other number, e-mail and notes.
  • Search by name, company or number. Click a number to call it: your own phone rings first, then the number is called.
  • Import a CSV file with a header row: name, company, work, mobile, other, email, notes (Dutch column names and ; work too). Choose Replace the whole phone book or add and skip duplicates.
  • Export the phone book as CSV.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Effect Include extensions Colleagues appear in the phone book with their extension Show names of incoming callers When a caller's number is in the phone book, the phone shows the name Phone book on the phones (XML) Yealink, Snom, Grandstream and Fanvil get the phone book through provisioning LDAP directory For phones and programs that look up names over LDAP (389, LDAPS 636). Only reachable from your own network; optionally with a password (the provisioning user)

The settings card shows the server, base DN, bind DN and search filter to enter on a phone or program that uses LDAP.

With linked systems the extensions of the other sites are part of the phone book too.

docs.title: Phones and provisioning
docs.text: Kiestoon configures desk phones for you: accounts, keys, language, time server, phone book and firmware. A phone only needs to know where Kiestoon is. You then link it to an extension in the portal.

docs.title: Supported brands
docs.text:
Brand Models Status Yealink T3x, T4xU, T5xW, with EXP40, EXP43 and EXP50 modules Tested Snom D7xx, D8xx, with D7 module Tested Grandstream GRP26xx, GXP2170, with GBX20 module Built after the vendor documentation Fanvil X3U, X4U, X5U and more Built after the vendor documentation Gigaset N670 / N870 IP PRO DECT, with several handsets Built after the vendor documentation Poly VVX, Edge E Built after the vendor documentation Htek, Akuvox, Cisco 8800 (3PCC firmware) Built after the vendor documentation

Brands marked "built after the vendor documentation" have not been tested on a real device yet. Let us know when something does not work.

docs.title: 1. Switch provisioning on
docs.text:
Open Phones & provisioning and click Provisioning settings:

Field What Provisioning on Phones may fetch their configuration Server address for phones Host name or IP address phones use to reach Kiestoon Username / Password Protect the provisioning address. Generated; keep them private Phone admin password Replaces the factory password of the phone's own web interface: Unique per phone (default) or Same for all phones. See below Time server NTP server for the phones, for example nl.pool.ntp.org Language Language on the phone display. Like the system follows the caller language

The card then shows the provisioning URLs to copy:

  • http://user:password@<server>:8080/prov/ for Yealink, Grandstream, Fanvil, Poly, Htek, Akuvox and Cisco,
  • the same address with snom{model}.htm for Snom,
  • the same address with gigaset/ for the Gigaset base station.

docs.title: 2. Point the phones at Kiestoon
docs.text:
Pick what suits your network:

  • DHCP option 66 on your router or DHCP server, with the URL above. New phones find Kiestoon by themselves.
  • By hand in the phone's web interface (Auto provisioning / Setting server).
  • Zero-touch through the vendor's redirection service, also for phones outside the office. See below.

docs.title: 3. Link a phone to an extension
docs.text:
A phone that asks for its configuration, but whose MAC address is unknown, appears under Waiting for an extension, with its brand and model recognised from what it sent. Choose an extension and click Link.

Kiestoon writes the configuration and sends the vendor's SIP NOTIFY (check-sync; resync for Cisco), so a registered phone fetches its new configuration within seconds. A phone that is not registered yet picks it up at its next provisioning check or right away after a reboot.

You can also add a phone in advance with Add phone (MAC address from the label at the back, model, extension and label), move a phone to another extension, or unlink it. Fetch configuration now asks a phone to reload. Preview config shows the exact file the phone gets.

docs.title: Multi-handset DECT (Gigaset)
docs.text: A Gigaset N670 or N870 base station carries several handsets. Handset 1 uses the extension of the phone; give each further handset its own extension under Handsets.

docs.title: Phone admin password
docs.text:
Provisioning replaces the factory password of every phone's own web interface (such as admin / admin). With Unique per phone (the default) Kiestoon makes a strong password for each phone; with Same for all phones every phone gets the password you enter under Provisioning settings.

Click the key icon of a phone in the list to see the user name (admin) and password, copy them and open the phone's web interface. A badge shows whether the phone already has the password: it gets it on its next check (after a reboot, a Resync or at night). New password makes a new one for that phone. Every look at a password and every new password is written to the audit log.

docs.title: Firmware
docs.text:
On the Firmware tab, upload the firmware once (or download it from a link to the vendor's site) and choose the models it is for. A .zip is unpacked. Click Roll out to phones: phones of those models install it on their next check, usually at night or after a reboot. Phones fetch it from Kiestoon (/prov/fw/<random token>/), so they need no internet access.

Warning

Only choose models a file is meant for. A wrong file can make a phone unusable.

docs.title: Newest firmware from the vendor
docs.text:
Above the firmware list, Newest firmware shows every phone model in use, the versions its phones run (read from the phone's user agent) and the newest version the vendor offers. Kiestoon looks this up:

  • Grandstream: on Grandstream's public firmware page.
  • Other brands: in the Kiestoon firmware catalog (packaging/firmware/catalog.json), with official download links of the vendors. Yealink, Snom and Poly have no public list Kiestoon can read, so this catalog is kept by hand. A model without an entry shows No source.

Click Roll out to download the newest version from the vendor and roll it out to all models it is meant for. A checksum in the catalog must match the download. Under Automatic updates choose:

Setting What happens every night at 04:00 Off Nothing Check and notify (default) Kiestoon checks and mails the notification address once per new version Roll out automatically Kiestoon downloads new firmware and rolls it out by itself, and mails what it did

You can point Kiestoon to your own catalog (same format) with Catalog address.

docs.title: Zero-touch provisioning
docs.text:
On the Zero-touch tab, Kiestoon shows the address to register with the vendor's redirection service. A new phone then asks that service where its settings are and configures itself out of the box, also at home.

  • Yealink RPS works automatically: enter an AccessKey ID and secret from the Yealink Device Management portal (API). Phones are registered and removed when you add or delete them.
  • Snom SRAPS, Grandstream GDMS, Fanvil FDPS, Htek, Poly, Gigaset and Cisco have no public API. Sign in to their portal, enter the server address shown, and import the MAC addresses with the MAC list (CSV) export.

Phones outside your network need HTTPS: switch on internet access or set a public address.

docs.title: Keys and expansion modules
docs.text: Every phone has a visual key editor with extra lines, BLF, speed dials, parking, intercom and expansion modules. That has its own chapter: Phone keys and modules.

docs.title: User portal
docs.text:
Every employee with a user account linked to an extension gets the user portal. It is the same address as the admin portal: Kiestoon shows the menu that fits the role. Employees manage their own phone here, without bothering the administrator.

Page What you do there My phone Do not disturb, forwarding, follow me, your own hours Voicemail Listen to messages, record greetings, change the PIN Queues & groups Sign in and out of queues, see your ring groups Colleagues See who is available, call, and transfer calls by drag and drop My calls Your own call history, call back with one click Softphone & devices Browser softphone, phone app with QR code, keys of your desk phone

docs.title: My phone
docs.text:
Setting What it does Do not disturb Callers hear busy or go to your voicemail. Also *76 on the phone. Forward to my mobile One click: every call goes to your mobile until you press Stop. Always forward to Your phone does not ring at all; calls go straight to this number. When busy, forward to When you are already on a call. When not answered, forward to After your ring time. Replaces voicemail.

A forward can go to a colleague, a ring group or an external number. External forwards use an outbound route, so the fraud protection limits still apply.

docs.title: Follow me
docs.text:
With Also ring other numbers your own phone rings first, then the numbers you add ring as well, for example your mobile and your home office phone.

  • Ring them after (seconds): 0 rings everything at once.
  • Ask to press 1: the person who answers has to press 1 first. This stops the voicemail of a mobile from taking the call.

docs.title: My hours
docs.text: Pick the time condition you follow under Follow the hours of, for example "Office hours". Outside those hours your calls go to Outside these hours, forward to, or to your voicemail when that is empty. Always available switches it off.

docs.title: Voicemail
docs.text: See Voicemail: messages, greetings and the PIN are all managed on this page.

docs.title: Queues & groups
docs.text: Sign in to the queues you are a member of, one by one or with Sign in to all / Sign out of all. Signed in means you receive callers from that queue. Fixed members are always signed in. On the desk phone *45 does the same. Under My ring groups you see the ring groups you are in and who in them is available.

docs.title: Colleagues and drag-and-drop transfer
docs.text:
The colleagues page shows every extension, ring group and queue with its live status: available, ringing, in a call or do not disturb. Click a colleague to call them. Call a number dials any number; with the softphone on the call starts in the browser, otherwise your desk phone rings first and sets up the call when you pick it up.

Transferring a call works the same for every employee:

  1. Answer the call on your desk phone or the softphone. It appears under My active calls.
  2. Choose Transfer directly (blind) or Ask first (attended).
  3. Drag the call onto a colleague, ring group or queue. Or press Transfer and pick a target; Esc cancels.
  4. With Ask first the caller waits on hold while you talk to the colleague. Then press Complete transfer, or Back to caller when the colleague cannot take it.

Reception

The switchboard works the same way, but shows every live call of the office instead of only your own.

docs.title: My calls
docs.text: Your own incoming, outgoing and missed calls, with Call back on every row. Administrators see all calls under Call history.

docs.title: Softphone & devices
docs.text:
Softphone in the browser. Press Turn on softphone and call and answer with any headset, right in the browser. The browser asks for the microphone once. The softphone keeps running while you use the rest of the portal and docks at the bottom of the screen. It needs https: open the portal through its internet address or your own reverse proxy. The administrator can switch the softphone off per extension.

Phone app. Show my settings shows the SIP account and a QR code for an app such as Linphone, Zoiper or Groundwire. Scan the code in the app and it is set up.

My desk phones. Phones that are provisioned for your extension appear here. Employees can set their own keys, for example a speed dial or a busy lamp field for a colleague. The phone picks up the new keys at its next restart or provisioning check.

Windows. For a full softphone in the taskbar, see the Windows softphone.

Mobile app. When your administrator allows it, Link mobile app shows a QR code for the Kiestoon app on your phone, see Mobile app.

docs.title: Voice prompts and speech
docs.text: Voice prompts are the announcements in IVR menus and queues: "Welcome to …", "All our colleagues are busy …". The built-in system prompts (voicemail, queue positions, numbers, dates) come in English and Dutch; your own prompts are made on this page or right inside the IVR builder.

docs.title: Add a prompt
docs.text:
Click New prompt, give it a name and choose one of:

  • Record in the browser with your microphone (needs the portal over https),
  • Upload an audio file (MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG),
  • Type the text, choose the engine and voice and click Generate audio (when text-to-speech or ElevenLabs is on, see below).

Audio is converted in the browser to telephone quality (8 kHz mono WAV). To rename a prompt, leave the audio empty.

docs.title: Prompt language
docs.text: The language of the built-in prompts is set under Settings › Calls › Language of prompts. Dutch prompts come from the kiestoon-sounds-nl package, spoken by an open (CC0) Piper voice. Anything without a Dutch version falls back to English.

docs.title: Speech
docs.text:
The Speech page (System menu) adds local speech technology: Piper and Whisper run on the server and no audio leaves it. Optional cloud voices are described under ElevenLabs voices.

Feature What it does Text-to-speech (Piper) Type the text of a menu or announcement and Kiestoon speaks it with a natural voice. Download at least one voice per language and pick the English voice and Dutch voice Speech-to-text (Whisper) Voicemail messages are transcribed and shown in the user portal and the voicemail e-mail (the mail can arrive up to a minute later)

Voices and models are downloaded from the portal with pinned SHA-256 checksums. Larger Whisper models are more accurate but slower; small is a good choice from 2 CPU cores. Speech needs the kiestoon-speech package (apt install kiestoon-speech, about 66 MB).

Summaries of calls and voicemail with a local model or Claude are on the AI summaries page.

docs.title: ElevenLabs voices
docs.text:
Next to the local Piper voices, Kiestoon can have prompts spoken by ElevenLabs, a cloud service with very natural voices. It is off by default and needs your own ElevenLabs account.

  1. Create an API key at elevenlabs.io under Developers › API keys, with access to text-to-speech and voices.
  2. Open Speech, switch on Use ElevenLabs, paste the key and click Check and save key. The key is checked with ElevenLabs, stored encrypted on the server and never shown again.
  3. Under Voice profile, choose the Dutch voice and English voice, and set Engine to ElevenLabs to use it by default. Switch on Lock the voice profile to fix the voice for every prompt (see below).

Choose a voice shows the ElevenLabs voice library and the voices in your account. It is filtered on the language of the PBX (Settings › Calls › Language of prompts), so a Dutch PBX shows Dutch voices first. Filter on gender, use and accent, and click the play button to hear a free sample. A library voice is added to your ElevenLabs account when you use it.

In the IVR builder and on this page, Generate starts with the voice of the profile and lets you choose another engine or voice for one prompt, unless the profile is locked. The counter under the text shows how many characters it costs and how many are left this period.

Good to know:

  • Only the typed text goes to ElevenLabs. Callers, recordings and voicemail never leave the server.
  • The audio is converted to 8 kHz WAV and stored on the server, so calls never wait for ElevenLabs and keep working without internet.
  • The same text with the same voice and settings is reused from the server and costs no new characters.
  • Use Piper when ElevenLabs cannot be reached keeps generating working when the key, the credits or the internet are gone (needs Piper switched on with a voice).
  • The admins get a mail (to the notification address of the mail server) when 80% of the characters of the period are used.
  • Model: Multilingual v2 sounds the most natural in Dutch; Flash v2.5 is faster and costs half the characters.

docs.title: Voice profile
docs.text:
The Voice profile card on the Speech page, under the API key, holds everything ElevenLabs uses to speak a prompt: the Dutch voice and English voice, the Model and the voice settings.

Setting What it does Stability Higher sounds steadier; lower sounds livelier. Similarity How closely the result follows the original voice. 75% is a good start. Style exaggeration Adds expression. Keep it at 0% for calm menu announcements. Speed 95% is a little slower than normal, pleasant for menu choices. Speaker boost Makes the voice a little clearer. Recommended on the phone.

Switch on Lock the voice profile so all prompts sound like the same speaker. Every Generate button (the IVR builder, this page and Generate again with this voice) then uses the profile's voice for the language of the text, with these settings; the engine and voice choice is replaced by the locked profile with a link back here. The lock needs ElevenLabs switched on, a saved key and at least one voice. When a language has no voice in the profile, the other voice speaks it. Switching ElevenLabs off releases the lock.

docs.title: Another voice for all prompts
docs.text: Prompts made from text remember their text and voice (the Source column). Tick them on this page, choose an engine and voice, and click Generate again with this voice to speak them all again, for example after choosing a new house voice. Recorded and uploaded prompts cannot be ticked.

docs.title: Call queues
docs.text: A call queue lets callers wait in line, with music and position announcements, until an agent is free. Calls are spread over the agents by a distribution strategy. Numbers are in the 700 range by default.

docs.title: Create a queue
docs.text:
1. Open Call queues and click New queue.

  2. Pick a distribution:

    Distribution Who rings Round robin Agents take turns, starting after the last one who got a call Ring all All free agents at once Longest idle The agent who has been idle longest Fewest calls The agent with the fewest calls today Random A random free agent In order Agents in a fixed order Random by penalty Random, a higher penalty gives a lower chance

  3. Add agents. Dynamic agents sign in and out themselves (user portal, desktop softphone or *45); agents set to Always on are always signed in. A penalty puts an agent further back.

  4. Optional: a greeting (a voice prompt played once when the caller enters), music on hold and announce position every N seconds. Callers hear the announcements in the caller language; Caller language on the queue sets it apart.
  5. Set the timings and limits, and when the queue is full or too slow: the overflow destination.

You can also change a queue, or create a new one, straight from the IVR builder: click a queue step on the canvas.

docs.title: Timings and limits
docs.text: Setting Meaning Ring an agent for Seconds an agent rings before the next one is tried Wait before the next agent Pause between two attempts Wrap-up time Seconds after a call before the agent gets the next one Maximum wait After this the caller goes to the overflow destination Maximum callers More callers go straight to the overflow (0 is unlimited) Accept callers when no agent is signed in Off: callers go straight to the overflow destination Record queue calls Every answered call in this queue is recorded

docs.title: Callback from the queue
docs.text:
Turn on Queue callback and waiting callers regularly hear that they can press 1 to be called back. They confirm their number (or type another one followed by #) and hang up. They keep their place in the queue: a placeholder waits for them. As soon as an agent is free, that agent's phone rings first (the display shows CB and the caller), the agent hears a short message and Kiestoon calls the caller through the outbound routes.

Setting Meaning Offer every How often waiting callers hear the offer Extra attempts How many more times Kiestoon tries when the caller does not answer (a retry goes to the front of the queue) Time between attempts Wait before the next attempt Give up after Minutes after the request after which an unanswered callback stops Caller ID for callbacks The number the caller sees; empty uses the outbound route

The open callbacks are on the switchboard, where reception can cancel one, try again or add a callback by hand (for example after a missed call).

Note

Callers with a hidden number are asked to type their number. Callbacks that were waiting when Kiestoon or Asterisk restarts are placed back in the queue; a callback that was being dialled at that moment is marked Not reached and can be tried again.

docs.title: Supervision: listen, whisper, barge in
docs.text:
With Supervision on, users with the role Reception or higher who have their own extension can join queue calls of that queue:

Mode Switchboard Phone Who hears the supervisor Listen ear button *33<extension> nobody Whisper (coach) speech button *34<extension> only the agent Barge in people button *35<extension> agent and caller

On the switchboard the buttons appear next to an agent who is in a queue call; your own phone rings and you are connected. During the call, press 4 to listen, 5 to whisper and 6 to barge in. Only queue calls can be joined, never other calls of the agent, and every use is written to the audit log.

Privacy

Listening in on calls is processing of personal data. Tell your employees (and, where needed, callers) that calls in this queue can be listened to, for example in the greeting and in your privacy policy.

docs.title: External numbers
docs.text: Under Agents, External numbers adds numbers outside the PBX that take calls like an agent, for example a mobile or another office. Type a name and number or pick one From the phone book. The queue rings them over the trunk, so every call uses an outside line. Untick a number to keep it in the list without ringing it. Up to 20 per queue.

docs.title: Agents on other sites
docs.text: With linked systems, agents of another Kiestoon can join the queue (Agents on linked systems). Their phones ring through the tunnel and their busy lamp tells the queue when they are in a call.

docs.title: Following a queue live
docs.text:
• The Call queues page shows waiting callers and signed-in agents.
  • The wallboard is a big-screen view for the team.
  • The switchboard lets reception sign agents in and out and pause them.
  • Agents use Queues & groups in the user portal or *45 / *45<queue> on the phone.

docs.title: Own reverse proxy
docs.text: Kiestoon can put itself on the internet with Caddy and a Let's Encrypt certificate (Internet access). When you already have a reverse proxy or load balancer (nginx, Traefik, HAProxy, a firewall with a web proxy), keep that switched off and let your proxy forward to Kiestoon instead.

docs.title: 1. Tell Kiestoon which proxy to trust
docs.text:
Go to Internet access › Own reverse proxy:

  1. Switch on Trust my reverse proxy.
  2. Enter the IP address of the proxy (or the range of a proxy cluster), one per line. Kiestoon only reads X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto from these addresses. From any other address the headers are ignored, so nobody can fake their address to get around the sign-in lockout or the firewall.
  3. Enter the public address, such as https://pbx.example.com. Kiestoon uses it in e-mails, for zero-touch provisioning and for the firmware links it gives phones.
  4. Save, then open the portal through the proxy. The box What Kiestoon sees now must show your own address as "Your address" and HTTPS as the connection.

Rules Kiestoon follows:

  • X-Forwarded-For is read from right to left; trusted proxies are skipped and the first other address is the client. A chain of proxies works when all of them are in the list.
  • Requests from 127.0.0.1 and ::1 are always trusted (a proxy on the same server).
  • A range of /0 (everything) is refused.

docs.title: 2. Forward to Kiestoon
docs.text:
Forward to http://<kiestoon>:8080 on your own network, or to https://<kiestoon>:8443 (self-signed certificate) when the network between proxy and Kiestoon is not trusted.

Your proxy must:

  • set X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto;
  • pass the Host header unchanged (passkeys and single sign-on check it);
  • forward WebSockets on /api/webrtc/ws, for the browser softphone;
  • allow uploads of up to 1 GB on /api/firmware/upload and 16 MB elsewhere, with a long timeout (firmware uploads can take minutes).

docs.title: nginx
docs.text:
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name pbx.example.com;
    ssl_certificate     /etc/ssl/pbx.example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/pbx.example.com/privkey.pem;

    client_max_body_size 1g;
    proxy_read_timeout   3600s;
    proxy_send_timeout   3600s;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://10.0.0.20:8080;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host              $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade           $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection        $connection_upgrade;
        proxy_buffering off;
        proxy_request_buffering off;
    }
}

# in the http block:
map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
    default upgrade;
    ''      close;
}

docs.title: Traefik (file provider)
docs.text:
http:
  routers:
    kiestoon:
      rule: Host(`pbx.example.com`)
      entryPoints: [websecure]
      tls:
        certResolver: letsencrypt
      service: kiestoon
  services:
    kiestoon:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: http://10.0.0.20:8080
        passHostHeader: true

Traefik sets X-Forwarded-* and forwards WebSockets by itself. Raise the timeouts of the entry point (respondingTimeouts.readTimeout) when you upload large firmware files.

docs.title: HAProxy
docs.text:
frontend https
    bind :443 ssl crt /etc/haproxy/certs/pbx.example.com.pem alpn h2,http/1.1
    http-request set-header X-Forwarded-Proto https
    option forwardfor
    timeout client 1h
    default_backend kiestoon

backend kiestoon
    timeout server 1h
    timeout tunnel 1h
    server pbx 10.0.0.20:8080 check

docs.title: Caddy on another server
docs.text:
pbx.example.com {
    reverse_proxy 10.0.0.20:8080
}

Caddy sets the headers and handles WebSockets by itself.

docs.title: 3. What does not go through the proxy
docs.text:
A web proxy only carries the portal, the softphone signalling and phone provisioning over HTTPS. Phones and trunks still reach Asterisk directly:

Port What 5060 UDP/TCP, 5061 TCP SIP (5061 is SIP over TLS) 10000–20000 UDP Audio (RTP)

Forward those on your router or firewall to Kiestoon, or keep phones on the local network or a VPN.

docs.title: Prometheus behind the proxy
docs.text:
/metrics goes through the proxy like every other path. Use the bearer token, or add the address of the Prometheus server to "allowed without a token". That list is checked against the client address Kiestoon derives from the trusted proxy, not against the proxy itself.

Two host names

Want a separate address for the employee portal, such as voipcentrale.example.com next to sip.example.com? Fill in Employee portal address too, see Separate host names.

docs.title: Ring groups
docs.text: A ring group rings a team on one number, for example sales or the warehouse. Numbers are in the 600 range by default.

docs.title: Create a ring group
docs.text:
1. Open Ring groups and click New ring group. The next free number is filled in.

  2. Choose the ring strategy:

    Strategy What happens All at once Every member rings at the same time. The first to answer gets the call One by one Members ring one after another, in the order of the list Rotating Like one by one, but each call starts at the next member Intercom (paging) Phones answer automatically on the speaker. Only for extensions; good for announcements

  3. Add members: extensions, and with Add an external number also a mobile phone (an external member costs an outgoing call).

  4. Ring time: how long the group rings (for one by one and rotating: per member).
  5. Caller ID prefix: shown before the caller's name, for example Sales:.
  6. Skip busy members: members who are already on a call do not ring.
  7. When nobody answers: any destination, for example a colleague's voicemail or a queue.

docs.title: Ring group or queue?
docs.text:
Ring group Call queue Callers wait No: when nobody answers, the call goes to the failover Yes, with music and position announcements Members Always on Agents sign in and out (or always on) Statistics and wallboard No Yes Best for Small teams, "ring everyone" Support desks, busy numbers

Employees see their ring groups and the status of the members in the user portal under Queues & groups.

docs.title: Inbound and outbound routes
docs.text: Routes decide where calls go: inbound routes send each of your phone numbers to a destination, outbound routes pick the trunk for numbers your users dial. Both are on Trunks & routes.

docs.title: Inbound routes
docs.text:
1. Open Trunks & routes › Inbound routes and click Add inbound route.
  2. Phone number: your number as the provider sends it. 0201234567, 31201234567 and +31201234567 are treated as the same number. Leave it empty for a catch-all route: every number that no other route matches.
  3. Send to: any destination, for example a time condition for your main number, a queue for a support number, an extension for a direct number or a fax box for your fax number.
  4. Caller name prefix (optional): shown before the caller's name on the phone display, for example Support:, so the person answering knows which number was called.

A typical setup

Number Send to Main number Time condition Office hours › IVR menu › ring group / queue Support number Call queue Support Direct numbers The employee's extension Fax number Fax box Empty (catch-all) Reception ring group

Calls from someone in the phone book show the contact's name.

docs.title: Route many numbers at once
docs.text: When your trunks have phone numbers, the numbers that do not have a route yet are listed above the routes. Tick the numbers (or Select all), click Route numbers, and choose one destination. Each number gets its own route, named after the name you give plus the number, so you can later send one of them somewhere else. When typing a phone number in a route, the trunk numbers are offered as suggestions.

docs.title: Outbound routes
docs.text:
Outbound routes are tried from top to bottom; the first route with a matching dial pattern is used. Use the arrows to change the order.

  1. Open Outbound routes and click Add outbound route.
  2. Click a preset: Dutch numbers (0[1-9]XXXXXXXX) or International (00X.), or write your own patterns.
  3. Add one or more trunks. They are tried in this order; the next trunk is used when one fails or is busy.
  4. Caller ID (optional) overrides the trunk's caller ID for this route. An extension's own outbound caller ID and the number of its extension group win over it.
  5. Who can use this route (optional): pick extension groups to give them their own route, for example over their own trunk. Others skip the route and take the next one that matches. Default: everyone.

docs.title: Dial patterns
docs.text:
Symbol Means X Any digit 0-9 Z 1-9 N 2-9 [1-5] A digit in the range . One or more digits

Each pattern has three parts: prefix (removed before dialing), pattern and prepend (added before dialing). Example: prefix 9, pattern 0XXXXXXXXX lets users dial 9 for an outside line.

docs.title: Who may call what
docs.text: Routes say how a number is dialed; the extension says whether it may be dialed. Each extension has an outbound class (internal only, national, international) and a switch for premium-rate numbers. On top of that the fraud protection limits concurrent outbound calls and sends alerts.

docs.title: Emergency calls
docs.text: 112 and 911 always work, from every extension, without a route, and even when a trunk limit or the fraud lock is active. Under Settings › Emergency calls you set the caller ID for emergency calls (a number tied to your address) and the order in which trunks are tried.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Settings holds the system-wide choices: the caller language, the number plan, emergency calls, network and the phone engine.

docs.title: Caller language
docs.text:
One setting for everything callers hear and phones show, in English or Dutch:

  • queue announcements: the position of the caller ("you are caller number 3") and the hold time,
  • voicemail menus and greetings, feature codes and other system messages,
  • numbers, dates and times that are spoken,
  • the default language of spoken text for IVR menus and voice prompts,
  • voicemail, fax and other system e-mails,
  • new users and their welcome e-mail.

Phone screens follow the caller language gives provisioned phones the same language at their next configuration update. Turn it off to keep a separate phone language under Phones & provisioning > Provisioning settings.

The language of the web interface is not part of it: every user chooses their own under Account. An administrator can work in English while callers hear Dutch.

A single queue or IVR menu can use another language in its own settings (Caller language), for example an English line for foreign customers. The language chosen during the first setup is the first caller language.

docs.title: Number plan
docs.text:
Kiestoon uses fixed ranges per purpose, shown in the table: extensions, ring groups, call queues, conference rooms, voicemail and features, and the emergency numbers.

Change number length switches between 3, 4 or 5 digit internal numbers. Existing extensions are renumbered automatically. Provisioned phones pick up their new number by themselves; other phones must be changed by hand. Kiestoon shows the numbers that cannot be shortened before you switch.

docs.title: Emergency calls
docs.text:
112 and 911 always work, from every extension, without a route and even when a trunk limit is reached or the fraud protection blocks outbound calls.

  • Caller ID for emergency calls: a number on which you can be called back, tied to your address. Empty: the trunk's caller ID.
  • Trunk order for emergency calls: which trunk is tried first. No order set: every trunk is tried.

docs.title: Network and NAT
docs.text:
Setting What it does Public address Public IP or host name, when this server is behind NAT. Empty: no NAT. Local networks Networks that are not behind NAT, one per line. SIP port (UDP/TCP) Default 5060. SIP TLS port Default 5061. Audio ports from / to RTP range, default 10000–20000.

Changing a port needs a restart of the phone engine.

docs.title: Calls
docs.text: Setting What it does Time zone For time conditions, call history and schedules. Country code Without +; 31 is the Netherlands. Codecs for phones In order of preference, for example g722,alaw,ulaw. Show numbers in national format Shows +31 20 … as 020 …, so calling back works.

docs.title: Restart the phone engine
docs.text: Some changes take effect after a restart of the phone engine (Asterisk); the portal then shows a banner. When idle restarts as soon as no calls are active. Restart now ends every active call.

docs.title: Windows softphone
