docs.text: Kiestoon Softphone is a desktop app for Windows 10 and 11. It puts the phone in the taskbar: call with your headset, with your colleagues, phone book and queues at hand, and transfer calls by dragging them onto a colleague.

docs.title: What it can do
docs.text:
• Contacts: colleagues with live status (available, ringing, in a call, do not disturb), the shared phone book and your favourites. Search on name, number or company.
  • Calls: answer, decline, mute, hold, keypad and transfer. Drag the call onto a colleague to transfer it, Direct or Ask first, just like in the user portal.
  • Queues: sign in, sign out or pause per queue, with the number of waiting callers.
  • Voicemail and call history with call back.
  • Headset buttons: answer, hang up and mute with the buttons of Jabra, Poly/Plantronics, EPOS, Logitech and other USB headsets that offer call buttons. Headsets without call buttons, and Bluetooth headsets, are shown as "sound only" and work for calls.
  • Sound: choose the microphone, the speaker for calls, and where it rings, for example on your speakers while you talk on the headset. On System default, calls go to a plugged-in headset by themselves.
  • Windows integration: tray icon, incoming-call popup, notifications for missed calls and new voicemail, tel: and sip: links open in the softphone, and Start with Windows.
  • Updates: under Info the softphone checks for new versions and updates itself, on the Production or Testing channel.

docs.title: Install and link
docs.text:
1. Open the user portal and go to Softphone & devices.
  2. Click Download for Windows and run the installer (.msi). Every Kiestoon server serves the installer that matches its own version, at /download/kiestoon-softphone.msi.
  3. Click Link this computer. The softphone opens and links itself to your account. Did it not open by itself? Enter the code shown in the portal in the softphone. The code is valid for 10 minutes.

The softphone can also be set up from the app itself: on the welcome screen enter the Server address (and a Pairing code from the portal or the welcome e-mail, if you have one) and click Connect. Then sign in with your username and password, or choose Sign in with your browser (SSO) for single sign-on and passkeys. Your browser then hands the link to the softphone.

A linked softphone stays signed in for 30 days after its last use, and can only use the user portal functions of your own extension. Linking switches on the browser softphone (WebRTC) for your extension.

Servers with their own certificate

When the server has no public certificate yet, the portal shows the certificate fingerprint next to the code. The softphone pins exactly that certificate, so the connection stays encrypted and cannot be taken over. With internet access switched on, the Let's Encrypt certificate is used and nothing has to be pinned.

docs.title: For administrators
docs.text:
Open Windows softphone in the System menu. The page offers the MSI that comes with this server (version, size and SHA-256), its download address, the command for a silent install and the server address that employees enter in the app.

msiexec /i "Kiestoon-Softphone_<version>_x64.msi" /qn

The table Linked softphones lists every linked softphone with its employee and extension. Unlink ends its session (for example for a lost laptop); the softphone shows the link screen again.

  • The softphone uses the same WebRTC connection as the browser softphone: the server needs https with a hostname (see Internet access or own reverse proxy).
  • The MSI can be rolled out with Intune, Group Policy or any other software distribution.
  • Each release on GitHub contains the MSI and a SHA256SUMS file; the softphone checks the checksum before it updates.

docs.title: Switchboard and wallboard
docs.text: The Reception menu is for the reception and team leads (role Reception and up): the switchboard to handle calls live, the wallboard for a screen on the wall, plus fax, call history and recordings.

docs.title: Switchboard
docs.text:
The switchboard shows, live:

  • Day / night: every time condition with its switch code, set to Automatic, Forced open or Forced closed with one click.
  • My active calls: the calls on your own extension, ready to transfer.
  • Live calls: every call in progress, with both parties and the duration.
  • Queues: waiting callers (with the longest wait), answered and abandoned calls, and every agent. Sign agents in or out, pause and resume them.
  • Colleagues: the busy lamp field: available, ringing, in a call, on hold, do not disturb or offline.

docs.title: Transfer by drag and drop
docs.text:
Drag any live caller onto a colleague, ring group or queue to transfer the call there. For your own calls choose Transfer directly (blind) or Ask first (attended): the target is called while the caller waits on hold; then Complete transfer or go Back to caller.

No mouse? Press the Transfer button on a call and pick the target; Esc cancels. This also works on touch screens.

docs.title: Supervision
docs.text: Next to an agent in a queue call of a queue with supervision on, the buttons Listen, Whisper and Barge in appear. Your own phone rings; answer to join the call.

docs.title: Callbacks
docs.text: The Callbacks list shows the callers who asked a queue to call them back, with their status: Scheduled, Waiting in queue, Calling back (with the agent), Called back, Not reached or Cancelled. Cancel an open callback, try a failed one again, or add a callback by hand. See callback from the queue.

docs.title: Wallboard
docs.text: The wallboard shows the queues at a glance for the whole team: who is waiting, today's figures and service level, and every agent. Click Full screen for a screen on the wall. For a TV, make a TV link instead: it needs no sign-in. See Wallboard and SLA alerts.

docs.title: Microsoft Teams
docs.text: With Direct Routing, people who work in Microsoft Teams make and receive normal phone calls through Kiestoon and your own trunks. Kiestoon acts as the SBC (session border controller) of your Microsoft 365 tenant: Teams sends its calls to Kiestoon, and Kiestoon rings Teams users like any extension.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Internet access switched on, with Use the certificate for SIP. Microsoft only accepts a public certificate (Let's Encrypt is fine) with an RSA key; Kiestoon asks Let's Encrypt for RSA when the certificate is used for SIP.
  • A domain verified in Microsoft 365 for the SBC name (for example pbx.example.com on the verified domain example.com), with at least one licensed user on that domain.
  • A Teams Phone licence for every Teams user who calls through Kiestoon (in Microsoft 365 E5, or as an add-on).
  • The MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module and a Teams administrator account.

docs.title: Setting it up
docs.text:
1. Go to Telephony > Microsoft Teams and switch on Microsoft Teams Direct Routing. The SBC domain name is filled in from Internet access.
  2. Check the SIP TLS port (5067 by default). It is separate from the TLS port of the phones, because Microsoft needs the domain name in every SIP message. The firewall opens this port for Microsoft's address ranges only (52.112.0.0/14 and 52.122.0.0/15).
  3. Choose how outside calls from Teams go out: through the normal outbound routes, or through one trunk. Choose the caller ID: the user's own Teams number, or the caller ID of the route or trunk.
  4. Save, then restart the phone system once (Settings): Asterisk opens the new port only on a restart.
  5. Add the Teams users (below), then run the PowerShell script from the Microsoft 365 setup tab.

Setup progress on the overview shows what is still missing. Microsoft SIP proxies shows whether Kiestoon reaches Microsoft's three proxies (sip, sip2 and sip3.pstnhub.microsoft.com); calls go to the next one when one fails.

docs.title: Teams users
docs.text:
Each Teams user gets a phone number (E.164, for example +31 20 123 4567) and optionally an extension:

Rings on What happens Teams + desk phone Calls to the extension ring the desk phone, the softphone and Teams together. First to answer gets the call. Teams only Calls to the extension ring only in Teams. No extension Calls to the number ring in Teams, unless an inbound route sends that number elsewhere.

With an extension, Teams users call colleagues by extension number and show as that extension; queues, ring groups and the switchboard reach them like any other extension. Their outgoing rights (national, international) are the rights of the extension. Teams numbers without an extension may call out nationally. 112 always works.

docs.title: The PowerShell script
docs.text:
Kiestoon writes the script with your domain name, port and users. Copy or download it and run it in PowerShell:

Install-Module MicrosoftTeams     # once
.\kiestoon-teams.ps1

The script adds Kiestoon as PSTN gateway, a voice route that sends every number to Kiestoon, the voice routing policy "Kiestoon", and gives every user their number and the policy. It is safe to run again after you add or change users. Microsoft can take up to an hour before a new gateway or number works.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Certificate not ready: check Internet access. The certificate must cover the SBC domain name and use RSA. If it still uses ECDSA, save Internet access again so Let's Encrypt issues an RSA certificate.
  • Proxies unreachable: check that port 5067 (or your port) is forwarded to Kiestoon in your router, and that the phone system was restarted after switching Teams on.
  • In the Teams admin center, under Voice > Direct Routing, Microsoft shows the TLS and SIP OPTIONS status of the gateway.
  • Audio always flows through Microsoft's media processors (no media bypass); the RTP port range must be reachable.

docs.title: Time conditions and holidays
docs.text: A time condition sends calls one way during opening hours and another way outside them, with a separate destination for holidays and a day/night switch for the unexpected.

docs.title: Create a time condition
docs.text:
1. Open Time conditions and click New time condition.
  2. Give it a name, for example Office hours.
  3. Add the opening hours: days and a from/until time. A lunch break is a second range (for example 08:30-12:00 and 13:00-17:30). Times use the time zone in Settings.
  4. Choose the destinations: When open, When closed and optionally On holidays (empty: same as closed).
  5. Keep Closed on holidays on to use the holiday calendar.

docs.title: Day/night switch
docs.text:
Every time condition has a mode:

Mode Effect Automatic Follows the opening hours and holidays Forced open Always open, for example when you stay open late Forced closed Always closed, for example during an emergency or a company outing

Switch it on the Time conditions page, on the switchboard (reception), or with the switch code *28<id> from any phone; the code is shown on the time condition. Dialing the code again returns to automatic.

docs.title: Holidays
docs.text:
The Holidays tab holds the calendar used by all time conditions.

  • Dutch holidays: New Year's Day, Good Friday, Easter, King's Day, Liberation Day, Ascension Day, Whitsun, Christmas and Boxing Day. Dates move with Easter and are calculated every year. Switch off the ones you work on.
  • Own closing days: for example a company outing or the days between Christmas and New Year, once or every year.

docs.title: Using a time condition
docs.text: A time condition is a destination: put it behind an inbound route, inside an IVR menu (a time condition step with open and closed lines) or in another time condition. Employees can also use a time condition as their personal schedule in the user portal (forward when closed).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with the dashboard: it shows whether the phone engine runs, which trunks are online, how many phones are registered and any warning that needs attention.

Then look in Logs: the phone system log says why a trunk does not register, why a phone cannot sign in or why a call fails. A trunk that does not work shows the reason from the log in the trunk list.

docs.title: Phones
docs.text:
A phone does not register
  • Check the extension number and SIP password (Extensions › Edit, or the SIP details in the user portal).
  • Is the phone outside the office? Then its address must be allowed in the firewall: use the SIP whitelist, Allow SIP from local networks or an Edge for branch offices.
  • Look under Firewall › Blocked addresses: after too many wrong passwords fail2ban blocks the address. Unblock lifts it.
  • Geo-blocking can keep out a phone abroad.
A phone is not provisioned automatically
  • Point the phone at http://<server>:8080/prov/ (DHCP option 66, or the phone's own provisioning setting).
  • New phones appear under Waiting for an extension: choose an extension and click Link.
  • Check the provisioning username and password under Phones › Provisioning settings.
  • Preview config shows the exact file the phone gets.
One-way audio or no audio

Almost always NAT. Fill in the Public address and Local networks under Settings, and forward the audio ports (default UDP 10000–20000) to the server. Switch off "SIP ALG" on the router.

docs.title: Calls
docs.text:
Outbound calls fail
  • Is the trunk online on the dashboard? Check the trunk credentials and the provider's IP whitelist.
  • Does an outbound route match the dialled number, and may the extension dial it (Outbound calls on the extension)?
  • Did fraud protection block outbound calls? Then the dashboard and Call features & fraud show it, with an Unblock button.
Incoming calls do not arrive
  • Does the inbound route have the number exactly as the provider sends it? The trunk setting Called number comes from decides where Kiestoon reads the number.
  • Check the time condition: maybe the call goes to the closed destination, or the mode is forced to night.
Callers hear English prompts

Set Language of prompts to Dutch under Settings, and check the language of IVR and queue prompts under Voice prompts.

docs.title: Portal and softphone
docs.text:
The browser softphone says 'Needs https'

Browsers only allow the microphone over https. Open the portal through its internet address or a reverse proxy, not via http://<ip>:8080.

Passkeys cannot be added

Passkeys need https and a host name, not an IP address.

I locked myself out with the firewall

Safe mode undoes a change within 90 seconds when you cannot reach the portal. Locked out anyway? On the server console, nft delete table inet kiestoon removes the Kiestoon rules until the next change in the portal.

I lost my MFA phone

Sign in with one of your recovery codes. Another administrator can also use Reset MFA under Users & roles.

docs.title: Mail and backups
docs.text:
No voicemail e-mails

Send a test under Mail server and check Recent e-mails for the error. Check that the extension has an e-mail address and Send voicemail to e-mail on.

A backup failed

Recent backups shows the error. Click Test on the location: often it is a changed password, a full disk or a firewall in between.

docs.title: Logs on the server
docs.text:
What Command Portal journalctl -u kiestoon -f Phone engine journalctl -u asterisk -f, or asterisk -rvvv for the live console SIP registrations asterisk -rx "pjsip show contacts" Updates journalctl -u kiestoon-updater Firewall nft list ruleset fail2ban fail2ban-client status Version kiestoon version First user name and password sudo kiestoon initial-admin

Still stuck? Open an issue on GitHub with the version and what you see in the logs. Remove passwords and phone numbers first.

docs.title: Trunks
docs.text: A trunk connects Kiestoon to your telecom provider, so you can call outside and receive calls on your phone numbers. You can have several trunks, for example a main provider and a backup.

docs.title: Add a trunk
docs.text:
1. Open Trunks & routes › Trunks and click Add trunk.
  2. Choose the provider. A template fills in the server, port, transport, codecs and the provider's IP ranges, and shows a step-by-step guide in the form when there is one.
  3. Fill in the account details from your provider and save. Within a minute the status turns Registered (registration) or Reachable (IP authentication).

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: Template Authentication Notes Voys Registration ha.voys.nl with DNS SRV failover. Full guide VoIPGRID platform (Spitsgroep, partners) Registration Create a VoIP trunk in their portal and use the server they give you KPN SIP trunk IP address KPN SBC 213.162.171.164 (+ .180), TCP. Full guide Cheapconnect Registration sip.cheapconnect.net. Full guide Speakup Registration sip.speakup.nl. Full guide Vodafone Ziggo Zakelijk Registration trunk.sipnl.net. Full guide Telnyx Registration Credential connection; TLS on port 5061 recommended Twilio Elastic SIP IP address Add the public IP of this server to the trunk's access control list Generic (registration) Registration Any provider that gives a username and password Generic (IP authentication) IP address Ask the provider which IP addresses they send calls from

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field What Authentication Registration: Kiestoon signs in with a username and password. IP address: the provider recognises your server by its public IP Host / Port The provider's SIP server. Port 0 follows the DNS SRV records of the host (recommended for Voys) Transport UDP, TCP or TLS Username / Password From your provider. Authentication username only when the provider gives a separate one From domain / From user Only when the provider asks for them Provider IP addresses Calls from these addresses are accepted as calls from this trunk, and the firewall lets them in Called number comes from Request URI or To header: where the provider puts your number on incoming calls Codecs In order of preference, for example alaw,g722 Maximum simultaneous calls 0 means no limit Caller ID Default number shown to people you call. Must be one of your own numbers Encrypt audio (SRTP) When the provider supports it, with TLS T.38 fax Receive and send faxes with T.38 when the provider offers it; otherwise fax goes over G.711

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The trunk list and the dashboard show the status of every trunk: Registered, Reachable, Not registered, Rejected (wrong username or password) or Unreachable. A trunk that is offline shows a warning at the top of the dashboard.

When a trunk is not registered or not reachable, the reason from the phone system log is shown under the status, for example Sign-in refused (401): the user name or password is wrong or The provider does not answer. Show log lines opens what to check and the log lines about the trunk. See Logs.

docs.title: Refresh registration
docs.text:
A trunk that signs in with a username and password has a Refresh registration button (the round arrows) in the trunk list. It makes Kiestoon sign in at the provider again right away, instead of waiting for the next retry. Use it after you changed something at the provider, after an outage, or when the status stays Rejected or Not registered. Kiestoon waits a few seconds for the provider's answer and shows it under the status:

Message Meaning Registered again just now The provider accepted the registration The provider rejected the registration Check the username and password with your provider Sent, the provider has not answered yet The status in the list updates by itself as soon as the answer comes

The button is not there for a trunk with IP authentication (there is nothing to sign in) or a trunk that is turned off.

docs.title: Phone numbers
docs.text:
Under Phone numbers in the trunk form you note which numbers the provider delivers on this trunk. You can add:

  • A number block: fill in the first number and the last number (050 700 1200 to 050 700 1259) or the first number and a count (050 700 1200 and 60). The form shows how many numbers that makes before you add them.
  • One or more numbers: paste a list, one per line or separated by commas.

Numbers keep their leading zero or +. A number can belong to one trunk only, and a trunk holds at most 10,000 numbers. Remove a single number with its cross, or all of them with Remove all.

The numbers are then offered wherever you choose a number:

  • under Inbound routes, where numbers without a route are listed and can be sent to an extension, IVR menu, queue, ring group or any other destination in one go (inbound routes);
  • as suggestions for the caller ID of a trunk, an outbound route and an extension.

docs.title: Behind NAT
docs.text: When Kiestoon has a private IP address, fill in the public address and the local networks under Settings › Network and NAT, and forward the SIP port and the RTP range (10000-20000/udp) to the server. Without that, calls connect but you hear nothing or only one side.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Calls on your numbers need an inbound route; calling out needs an outbound route.

docs.title: Updates and channels
docs.text: Kiestoon updates itself from the portal. Every release is published on GitHub with its .deb packages, LXC templates, the Windows softphone and a SHA256SUMS file.

docs.title: Info & updates
docs.text:
The Info & updates button at the bottom of the menu shows the version, commit, build date, host name, uptime and update channel.

  1. Click Check for updates. Kiestoon asks GitHub for the newest release on your channel.
  2. When a newer version is available, read the Release notes and click Update now.
  3. Kiestoon makes a backup, installs the new version and restarts. The portal is unavailable for about a minute and comes back by itself. Calls in progress are dropped, so update outside office hours.

Only administrators can change the channel or update.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Channel What you get Production Stable releases (v0.6.0). Recommended. Testing Release candidates (v0.6.0-rc.12), to try new features before everyone else.

The channel is switched in the same window. Going from Testing back to Production can mean that the newest production version is older than the one you run; Kiestoon then says so and lets you install it.

The menu always shows the channel with a coloured dot: green for production, orange for testing.

docs.title: What happens during an update
docs.text:
The update runs as a separate system service (kiestoon-updater), so it survives the restart of the portal:

  1. It downloads the packages and SHA256SUMS from the GitHub release and checks the checksums.
  2. It stops the portal and backs up the data directory to /var/lib/kiestoon-backups (the newest 5 are kept).
  3. It installs the packages, which restarts the portal and applies the new configuration.

When something fails, the window shows the error and the backup it made. Updates do not replace your backups to a remote location; keep those running as well.

docs.title: Updating by hand
docs.text: On the command line, install a downloaded package with apt install ./kiestoon_<version>_amd64.deb. For branch office edges that is the way to update.

docs.title: Updating a high-availability pair
docs.text: Update the standby first, then click Switch over, then update the old primary. See High availability.

docs.title: Users, roles and sign-in
docs.text: Everyone who opens the portal signs in with their own account. The role of the account decides what they see.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role What they can do Super admin Full control, including other super admins. Administrator Manages the phone system. Must use two-factor authentication. Reception Sees live calls and queues, signs agents in and out, switches day and night mode, uses the switchboard and wallboard. User Manages their own phone in the user portal.

An account linked to an extension also gets the user portal of that extension, whatever its role. An administrator with an extension sees both menus.

docs.title: Add employees
docs.text:
There are two ways:

  • With the extension. In the extension form, switch on Create a portal account and send a welcome e-mail. The employee gets an e-mail with a link to set a password (valid for 72 hours), the portal address and the details for a softphone app. No password is ever sent by e-mail. Send welcome e-mail sends a new link later.
  • Under Users & roles › New user, with a username, full name, e-mail, role and optionally an extension. Leave the password empty for accounts that only use single sign-on.

A disabled account cannot sign in. Reset MFA switches off the second factor of an account, for example after a lost phone; the person sets it up again at the next sign-in.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication (MFA)
docs.text:
Administrators and super admins must use a second factor. At their first sign-in Kiestoon shows a QR code for an authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator, 1Password, Bitwarden…). After confirming the first code they get recovery codes: each works once, for when the phone is lost. Store them in a password manager.

A passkey, or single sign-on with Trust the provider's MFA, counts as the second factor as well.

From a trusted network, such as the office LAN, the MFA step can be skipped for the roles you choose.

docs.title: Passkeys
docs.text: Under My account › Passkeys everybody can add a passkey: sign in with a fingerprint, face or device PIN instead of a password. Passkeys only work over https with a host name (for example https://pbx.example.com), not with an IP address. See Internet access.

docs.title: Single sign-on
docs.text:
Under Single sign-on › New provider you connect an identity provider. The sign-in page then shows a button "Sign in with …".

Provider Issuer URL Microsoft Entra ID https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0 Google Workspace Fixed for Google Keycloak Your Keycloak address with the realm name authentik Ends with the slug of the application Other (OpenID Connect) The address that serves /.well-known/openid-configuration SAML 2.0 The metadata URL of the identity provider

docs.title: Microsoft Entra ID step by step
docs.text:
1. In the Entra admin center, go to App registrations › New registration.
  2. Add the Redirect URI that Kiestoon shows, with type Web.
  3. Create a client secret under Certificates & secrets.
  4. Under Token configuration, add a groups claim (security groups).
  5. In Kiestoon, fill in the tenant ID in the issuer URL, the Client ID (application ID) and the Client secret.
  6. Under Role mapping, map groups to roles. For Entra ID use the group's object ID. Members get the role of their group; the highest role wins.
  7. Choose the Role without a matching group: a role, or No access to refuse everyone outside the groups.

Other options:

  • Create accounts automatically: at the first sign-in. Off: an administrator creates the account first, with the same e-mail address.
  • Trust the provider's MFA: administrators who signed in with SSO need no second Kiestoon code. Enforce MFA at the provider then, for example with Conditional Access.

For SAML 2.0, give the identity provider the SAML entity ID / metadata and the SAML reply URL (ACS) that Kiestoon shows, and fill in the metadata URL (or paste the XML). Groups come from the Groups attribute.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text: The Audit log shows the last 200 events, with time, user and IP address: every sign-in and failed attempt, every change to the configuration, and sensitive actions such as playing a recording, exporting call history, revealing the backup key, a restore, an update or a fraud alert.

docs.title: Voicemail
docs.text: Every extension can have a voicemail box. Callers leave a message when nobody answers, when the line is busy, or when a route or IVR sends them straight to voicemail.

docs.title: Switch it on
docs.text:
In the extension form (see Extensions):

  • Voicemail on, with a PIN of 4-8 digits (generated when empty).
  • Send voicemail to e-mail: the message arrives as an audio attachment, with the caller, time and length. Needs an e-mail address on the extension and a mail server.
  • Delete after sending: the message is then only kept in the e-mail.

With speech-to-text on, the e-mail and the portal also show a transcription of the message.

docs.title: Listen
docs.text: Where How User portal › Voicemail Play messages in the browser, mark them as heard, delete them Phone Dial *97 from your own phone, or the voicemail key Any phone Dial *98, enter the mailbox number and PIN E-mail The audio attachment

docs.title: Greetings
docs.text:
In User portal › Voicemail › Greetings employees record their own greetings in the browser:

Greeting Played Not available When you do not answer Busy When you are on another call Name Your name, used in standard messages Temporary Overrides the others while it exists, for example during a holiday

Without an own greeting callers hear a standard message with the extension number, in the prompt language from Settings. The PIN can be changed on the same page.

docs.title: Wallboard, SLA alerts and reports
docs.text: The wallboard shows your queues in large print for a screen on the wall: who is waiting, how long, today's service level and what every agent is doing. Kiestoon watches the thresholds you set per queue and warns the team when a queue gets into trouble.

docs.title: What the wallboard shows
docs.text:
Each queue gets a tile with:

  • Waiting: callers in the queue now, including callbacks (shown in purple, with the time since they asked).
  • Longest wait: the caller who has waited longest. It turns red above the queue's maximum wait.
  • Service level: the ring shows the share of today's calls answered within the target time. Green at or above the norm, orange up to 10 points below it, red below that.
  • The callers in order, and at the bottom today's answered calls, hung up calls, average wait and average call.

The Agents panel lists everyone signed in to the queues, with a timer since their last change: in a call (with the queue and caller), ringing, internal call, free (with today's number of calls), paused or offline. Below the queues a chart shows the calls answered and hung up per hour today.

How the service level is counted

Answered within the target time, divided by answered plus hung up calls. Callers who hang up within 5 seconds don't count (they most likely dialled the wrong number), nor do callers who left to the overflow or asked to be called back. The figures start at midnight and are kept for 400 days for reports.

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
The wallboard has three layouts:

Layout Shows Overview All queues, the agents and the calls per hour One queue large One queue at a time with its agents; with several queues it steps through them Agents A card per agent with state and timer

In the portal you choose the layout at the top of Reception › Wallboard, or Rotate to switch every 30 seconds. Supervisors with their own extension see the listen, whisper and barge buttons next to an agent in a call (for queues with supervision on). On a TV link the layouts and the switch interval are part of the link.

docs.title: TV links
docs.text:
A TV does not sign in. As an administrator, open Reception › Wallboard › Settings and click New TV link. You choose:

  • a name, for example Support room;
  • the queues to show (or all queues);
  • the layouts and how often to switch between them;
  • the theme, dark or light (light works better in rooms with a lot of daylight);
  • Hide caller names: shows only the last 4 digits of numbers, for a screen visitors can see.

Copy the link and open it on the TV, a Chromecast, a Fire TV stick or a mini PC with a browser, in full screen. The link looks like https://pbx.example.com/wall/k7Q2m-X9vLr-3e8sW-dPz4a. The key in it is the secret: anyone with the link sees the wallboard (and nothing else). New key replaces the key, so the old link stops working; Revoke removes the link. Last shown tells you when a screen last fetched the figures.

Keep the screen on

The TV page asks the browser to keep the screen awake. Set the TV or stick itself not to go to sleep as well.

docs.title: Design your own screen
docs.text:
Every TV link can get a design of its own in the wallboard designer: go to Wallboard → Settings and click Design on a screen.

Layout. Drag tiles from the list on the left onto the grid (12 × 8 for a landscape screen, 6 × 12 for portrait), or click a tile to place it on the first free spot. Drag a tile to move it and pull its corner to resize it; with the keyboard, the arrow keys move the selected tile and Shift + arrows resize it. A screen can have several pages that rotate, each with its own time. Undo and redo keep the last 50 steps.

There are 17 tiles: a number (KPI), a service level gauge, a trend, a queue tile, waiting callers, compare queues, callback requests, an agent list, agent tiles, a leaderboard, calls per hour, answered / abandoned, a clock, a text, a news ticker, a logo or image, and SLA alerts.

Per tile you choose the title, the figure (live: waiting, longest wait, callbacks, agents free / on a call / paused; or over a period: offered, answered, abandoned, abandoned %, service level, average wait and talk time, longest wait), which queues it counts, the period (today, last hour, yesterday, last 7 days), and when it turns orange or red. Take over from the queue SLA uses the thresholds of the queue (see below). A red figure can blink, and a figure of today can show yesterday's value next to it.

House style & display. Per screen: dark, light or automatic theme (light from 07:00 to 19:00), an accent colour, the Kiestoon logo or your own logo, background, tile style, text size, density, what the header shows, the language of the screen, and what happens on an SLA alarm (red banner, a sound on the TV, jump to the page with the alarm). Start quickly from a template: overview, one queue large, agents, reception compact, contact centre KPI or blank. Powered by RHIS always stays visible.

Draft and publish. Save keeps your work as a draft. The TV only shows it after Publish. Preview shows the draft full screen with live figures. A screen without a published design keeps showing the classic layouts.

docs.title: A screen's own address
docs.text:
Besides the long secret link, every screen has an address you choose yourself, for example https://pbx.example.com/wall/reception. Set it under Address & access in the designer, and choose who may open it:

  • Everyone who knows the address: handy on your own network.
  • With a pin code: the TV asks for the pin code (4 to 10 digits) once and remembers it. New key logs out all TVs.
  • Nobody: the address is off; only the secret link works (the default for existing screens).

Under Only from these networks you can limit a screen to networks such as 192.168.10.0/24. That applies to both the own address and the secret link. The screen only ever receives figures of the queues you chose for it, and wrong addresses or pin codes count towards the same block as wrong provisioning requests.

docs.title: SLA thresholds
docs.text:
Under SLA thresholds per queue you set per queue:

Threshold Alert when Target time Not an alert itself: the time within which a call counts as answered on time (default 20 s) Service level norm Today's service level is under this percentage (judged from 5 calls) Max. waiting More callers are waiting than this Max. wait A caller has waited longer than this Max. hung up More than this share of today's callers hung up (judged from 10 calls)

Leave a threshold empty to not monitor it. The Now column shows whether the queue is within its thresholds.

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
Kiestoon checks the thresholds every 5 seconds. Under Alerts you choose where an alert goes:

  • On the wallboard and the switchboard: a red banner at the top and a red border around the queue.
  • By e-mail to the recipients, through the mail server. The quiet period (default 15 minutes) keeps the same alert of the same queue from being mailed more than once in that time.
  • Only mail during the opening hours of a time condition, so nobody gets mail at night.
  • Also mail when it is fine again sends a short mail when the queue is back within the threshold.

Push notifications in the mobile app follow with the app.

docs.title: Scheduled reports
docs.text:
Under Scheduled reports you make an overview that Kiestoon mails by itself. Click New report and choose:

Period Sent Covers Compared with Daily every day (or only workdays) at the time you choose that day the same day a week earlier Weekly on the day and time you choose the previous week, Monday to Sunday the week before Monthly on the 1st at the time you choose the previous month the month before

Choose the queues, the content (per queue, per agent, per hour, and the change against the period before), the recipients and the language (English or Dutch) of the mail.

The mail is a plain HTML mail that works in every mail program. At the top it shows the calls, service level, average wait and hung up share, each with the change against the period before. Below that the tables per queue, per agent and per hour, the busiest hour and the number of SLA alerts. The figures per day and queue and per agent are attached as a CSV file, which opens in Excel.

  • Preview shows the mail with the current figures.
  • Send now to me mails it to your own address (set it under Users).
  • A report that cannot be delivered is not retried every minute: it waits for its next send moment. The mail log shows what went wrong.

docs.title: Research: multi-tenant Kiestoon
docs.text: Status: research only (phase 4). Nothing in this document is built. It answers one question: what would it take for one Kiestoon installation to serve several organisations (tenants), for example a reseller with twenty small offices?

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Kiestoon is single-tenant by design: one organisation, one Asterisk, one SQLite database, all state in /var/lib/kiestoon. That keeps installation, backups and updates simple, and it is what most customers need.

There are three ways to serve several organisations. The recommendation is option B: one Kiestoon container per tenant, with a shared SIP edge (Kamailio) and a small management portal in front. It reuses everything Kiestoon already does, keeps tenants fully separated, and the extra work is mostly around the edges instead of inside every feature.

A. Tenants inside one Kiestoon B. One container per tenant + SIP edge C. Separate servers, no sharing Separation between tenants Logical (a tenant_id everywhere) Process, file system and database Complete Work in Kiestoon itself Very large: every table, dialplan context, API call and UI page Small: a few settings for running behind an edge None New components None Kamailio + RTPengine, management portal None Public IP addresses needed 1 1 1 per tenant Resources per tenant Lowest Roughly 150 MB RAM idle per container (estimate) A whole VM Backups and restore per tenant Hard (one database) Already works (per container) Already works Updates per tenant All at once Per tenant, staged Per tenant Risk of a bug leaking data between tenants Real Very low None

docs.title: Option A: tenants inside one installation
docs.text:
Every row in the database gets a tenant_id, every Asterisk object gets a tenant prefix (t12-201), every dialplan context is duplicated per tenant, and every API handler and UI page filters on the tenant of the signed-in user. Asterisk itself has no tenant concept, so separation is only as good as the generated configuration.

Problems found:

  • About 40 tables and roughly 300 API routes would need tenant filtering. One missed WHERE tenant_id = ? shows one customer's call history to another.
  • Feature codes, parking lots, pickup groups, conference numbers, voicemail contexts and music on hold all share one Asterisk namespace and must be prefixed and tested per tenant.
  • Restoring one tenant from a backup means extracting its rows from a shared database and a shared spool.
  • Reloading Asterisk for one tenant's change reloads it for everyone.
  • Phone provisioning uses one set of credentials; it would need one per tenant.

This is how FreePBX-style multi-tenant forks and FusionPBX (on FreeSWITCH, which has domains built in) work. For Kiestoon it would touch almost every file and would delay v1.0 by months. Not recommended.

docs.title: Option B: one container per tenant behind a shared SIP edge (recommended)
docs.text:
internet
                    |
     +--------------+---------------+
     |  Edge (one public IP)         |
     |  - Caddy: https://<tenant>.pbx.example.com -> container
     |  - Kamailio: SIP 5060/5061, routes on domain / DID
     |  - RTPengine: audio relay, one port range
     +--+-----------+-----------+----+
        |           |           |
   +----+---+  +----+---+  +----+---+
   | tenant | | tenant |  | tenant |   unchanged Kiestoon LXC containers,
   |   a    | |   b    |  |   c    |   private addresses (10.10.0.x)
   +--------+  +--------+  +--------+

docs.title: How the pieces fit
docs.text:
• Kiestoon containers. The LXC image Kiestoon already builds runs per tenant on a private network. Each keeps its own database, Asterisk, backups, update channel and admin accounts. Nothing inside changes.
  • Web. Caddy (or the reverse proxy support built in phase 4) routes https://<tenant>.pbx.example.com to the right container. Each container trusts the edge as its reverse proxy and uses its own public URL.
  • SIP signalling. Kamailio listens on the one public IP. Phones register as 201@a.pbx.example.com; Kamailio picks the container from the domain and forwards (it does not need to know the passwords; the container still authenticates). Kamailio adds Path headers so calls to the phone go back through the edge.
  • Trunks. Incoming calls from a provider are routed on the dialled number (DID) with a table in Kamailio (dispatcher or dialplan module, filled from the management portal). Each tenant can also keep its own trunk registration, which then goes out through the edge.
  • Audio. RTPengine relays the RTP between the internet and the containers, so only one public port range is needed and phones behind NAT keep working. It also bridges WebRTC (DTLS-SRTP) to plain RTP if the browser softphone should go through the edge instead of Caddy.
  • Provisioning and zero-touch. Phones get https://<tenant>.pbx.example.com/prov/ as their address, so the redirection services (Yealink RPS, Snom SRAPS and the others) already work per tenant.
  • Management portal. A small extra service creates and deletes tenant containers (lxc-copy of the image, or incus), fills the Kamailio routing tables, shows the status of every tenant and gives the reseller one sign-in that opens each tenant's Kiestoon with single sign-on (OIDC, already supported).

docs.title: Changes needed in Kiestoon
docs.text:
Small and contained:

  1. A setting "SIP edge": the address of the Kamailio host, trusted for Path/Record-Route, and the external address to advertise. Asterisk then uses the edge as outbound proxy for trunks and phones.
  2. Generating rtp.conf and PJSIP external_media_address for the edge case (RTP to RTPengine instead of the internet).
  3. A management API token per container so the portal can read status (the API tokens of phase 3 already cover this) and an endpoint that reports health and version (exists: /api/system/info, /metrics).
  4. Headless setup: create the first admin and SSO provider through the API when the container is created, so no setup token has to be copied by hand.

docs.title: Costs and limits
docs.text:
• Memory: an idle Kiestoon container is expected to use roughly 150 MB (to be measured before building). A server with 8 GB RAM and 4 cores comfortably runs 25 to 40 small tenants; concurrent calls, transcoding and speech-to-text set the real limit.
  • Kamailio and RTPengine are mature (used by most large carriers) but are a new skill set to operate. RTPengine needs a kernel module for best performance; the user-space mode is fine for a few hundred calls.
  • Updates still happen per container. The management portal can roll them out in waves.
  • Fax with T.38 through RTPengine works but needs testing with each provider.

docs.title: Rough effort
docs.text: Part Estimate Edge: Kamailio + RTPengine configuration, packaging, tests 3–4 weeks Kiestoon changes (edge setting, headless setup) 1 week Management portal (tenants, routing tables, status, SSO, updates) 3–4 weeks Load and failure testing 1–2 weeks

docs.title: Option C: separate servers
docs.text: Every customer gets their own Kiestoon VM or LXC container with its own public IP. This works today without any changes and is the right answer for a handful of customers. It stops scaling when IPv4 addresses, router port forwards and per-customer certificates become the bottleneck, which is exactly what option B solves.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
1. Ship v1.0 single-tenant as planned.
  2. For resellers with a few customers, use option C now (one LXC per customer).
  3. When there is demand for more, build option B as a separate product (working name "Kiestoon Host") in its own repository, with the small Kiestoon changes listed above in a minor release. The Kamailio + RTPengine work overlaps with Kiestoon Edge in phase 5, so build both on the same SIP edge component.
  4. Do not build option A.

docs.title: Open questions for Reinder
docs.text:
• Is the target a reseller hosting many customers, or one organisation with several departments? For departments, Kiestoon's existing features (separate ring groups, time conditions and trunks per number) may already be enough.
  • Should tenants be able to bring their own trunks, or does the reseller provide all numbers?
  • Is a separate repository and product name for the edge acceptable?

docs.title: Phase 0 build plan
docs.text:
Status: built. Everything below is implemented; kept as a record of the design.

Work in progress on branch feat/phase-0-foundation. PRs target testing; main is production. Branch flow: feature branch → PR into testing → CI green → merge → tag v0.1.0-rc.N on testing → after Reinder tests, merge testing into main and tag v0.1.0.

docs.title: Done on this branch
docs.text:
• ROADMAP.md, LICENSE (GPL-3.0), branding/ (tokens, README, Kiestoon mark)
  • server/ Go module (Go 1.26): internal/version, internal/config, internal/store (SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite, WAL, migrations with PRAGMA user_version), internal/auth (bcrypt cost 12, min 12 chars, sessions with sha256-hashed tokens, TOTP via pquerna/otp, 8 recovery codes, IP limiter)

docs.title: Backend (server/)
docs.text:
• internal/updates: query https://api.github.com/repos/<repo>/releases; channel production = newest non-prerelease, testing = newest including prereleases; compare with golang.org/x/mod/semver. Apply = write <DataDir>/update-request.json ({version, channel, requestedAt, requestedBy}); a root systemd path unit picks it up. Status from <DataDir>/update-status.json.
  • internal/api: chi router, JSON helpers, security headers (CSP default-src 'self', frame DENY, nosniff, referrer no-referrer), cookie kiestoon_session (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure when TLS or KIESTOON_SECURE_COOKIES=true). Mutating requests must have Content-Type: application/json. Endpoints:
  • GET /api/setup/status, POST /api/setup (only when no users; creates superadmin, logs in)
  • POST /api/auth/login → {mfaRequired}; POST /api/auth/mfa {code}; POST /api/auth/logout
  • GET /api/me → user + mfaEnrollmentRequired (admin without TOTP)
  • POST /api/account/mfa/enroll → {secret, otpauthUrl}; POST /api/account/mfa/confirm {code} → {recoveryCodes}
  • PUT /api/account/language {language}
  • PUT /api/account/theme {theme} (system | dark | light)
  • GET /api/system/info; PUT /api/system/channel {channel} (admin)
  • POST /api/system/updates/check; POST /api/system/updates/apply (admin); GET /api/system/updates/status
  • Admins without MFA get 403 mfa_enrollment_required on everything except me/enroll/confirm/logout/info.
  • Login limiter: 5 failures per IP per 10 minutes → 429. Audit log entries for login, MFA, channel, update.
  • internal/web: //go:embed all:dist, SPA fallback to index.html; make copies web/dist into it.
  • cmd/kiestoon/main.go: load config, open DB, hourly session purge, graceful shutdown.

docs.title: Frontend (web/)
docs.text: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind v4 (@tailwindcss/vite), react-router, i18next (en default, nl), lucide-react icons, qrcode for the TOTP QR, fonts bundled via @fontsource (Inter, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono). Look = the approved UI sketch https://claude.ai/artifact/UmKQFN3z6qx7Czwy6xthEm (dark, cyan/indigo, left menu, "Powered by RHIS" bottom-right with rhis-logo-wit.svg from the RHIS house style artifact https://claude.ai/artifact/JphZ8zRMCYKVhtPw69GkV3). Screens: setup wizard, login + MFA step, MFA enrollment (forced for admins, shows recovery codes), layout with full left menu (items for later phases open a "coming in phase N" page), dashboard skeleton, Info dialog (version, commit, channel switch, check for updates, update now, status).

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
• packaging/nfpm.yaml → .deb (binary in /usr/bin/kiestoon, systemd units, env file /etc/kiestoon/kiestoon.env, user kiestoon, data /var/lib/kiestoon)
  • packaging/systemd/: kiestoon.service (hardened), kiestoon-updater.path + .service, packaging/kiestoon-updater script (download .deb from release, pre-update tar.zst backup of data dir, apt install, restart, write status)
  • install.sh for Debian 13 (--channel production|testing)
  • lxc/build-lxc.sh: debootstrap trixie rootfs + .deb → Proxmox .tar.zst template
  • .github/workflows/ci.yml (go vet/test, web build, deb build) and release.yml (on tag v*: build, attach .deb + LXC template + checksums, prerelease when tag has -)

docs.title: Import from UniFi Talk
docs.text: Kiestoon can take over a UniFi Talk phone system from a Talk backup: the smart attendants (voice menus) with their recordings, the users with their extension, call groups, call queues, the SIP trunk and the phone numbers. The import runs on the Import page; see the import overview for the steps every system shares.

docs.title: 1. Make the backup in UniFi OS
docs.text:
1. Open the UniFi OS console (UDM, UDM Pro, UCG, Cloud Key or UniFi OS Server) where Talk runs.
  2. Go to Settings → Control Plane → Backups (older versions: System → Backups).
  3. Choose Download and pick the Talk application. You get a file like unifi_os_backup_for_talk_1795438324390_97bfc7f6.unifi.

A full console backup works too, as long as Talk is in it.

Keep the file safe

A UniFi OS backup also holds certificates, private keys and SIP passwords. UniFi encrypts it with a key that is the same on every console, so the file is effectively readable by anyone who has it. Kiestoon reads only the Talk part, keeps the file in memory for the preview and does not store it.

docs.title: 2. Upload and check the preview
docs.text:
Upload the .unifi file on the Import page. Kiestoon recognises it automatically and shows what it will create:

From Talk Becomes in Kiestoon User (extension, name, SIP password, voicemail on/off) Extension. The SIP password is kept when Kiestoon accepts it, so a phone only needs the new server address and number Call group (members, simultaneous or one by one, no-answer action) Ring group Call queue (agents, strategy, maximum wait, ring time, wrap-up, overflow to voicemail) Queue SIP gateway (provider, account, password, numbers) Trunk, with the matching Kiestoon provider template (for example Voys) Phone number and where it rings Inbound route Smart attendant with its keys, sub menus and recordings Voice menu in the IVR builder, one recording per step Global voicemail greeting Prompt

Every extension, group and queue gets a free number in your Kiestoon number plan. Talk numbers are kept when they fit (same length, right range); you can change every number in the preview. Things that already exist in Kiestoon with the same name are reused, so you can run the import again without getting duplicates.

docs.title: How the attendants are converted
docs.text:
• The welcome recording plays first, then the caller chooses a key, as in Talk.
  • A key with its own recording plays it and then goes to the user, group, queue or attendant it points to.
  • A key that opens a sub menu becomes a Choice menu step with its own keys.
  • "Press 9 to hear the menu again" built in Talk with an extra attendant that forwards back goes straight back to the main menu in Kiestoon; the extra attendant is not imported.
  • What happens when the caller presses nothing becomes the No choice step.
  • Recordings (MP3) are converted to telephone quality (8 kHz) in your browser and stored as prompts, named after the attendant and the step (for example Talk - IJRB V2 - Zwembad).

docs.title: 3. What is not imported
docs.text:
• Phones. Kiestoon provisions its own phones; add them on the Phones page. Phones that used a SIP account keep working once they point at Kiestoon with the new number and the same password.
  • Messages a queue plays before it sends callers on (for example "nobody is available"). They are imported as prompts, so you can use them in a voice menu.
  • Spoken (text-to-speech) attendant greetings without a recording: add a prompt, for example with text to speech.
  • Voicemail messages, call history, SMS, contacts and Talk-specific settings such as phone designs and paging.

After the import, check the voice menus in the IVR builder, make a test call (Test call in the builder) and move the numbers to the new trunk at your provider.

docs.title: Provider: Cheapconnect
docs.text: Cheapconnect is a Dutch VoIP provider with SIP accounts that work with your own phone system. Kiestoon has a ready-made Cheapconnect template.

docs.title: What the template sets
docs.text:
Setting Value Why Authentication Registration Cheapconnect only routes incoming calls to a registered PBX Host / port sip.cheapconnect.net, 5060 Cheapconnect's SIP server Transport UDP As in Cheapconnect's Asterisk example Codecs alaw,ulaw,g722 Cheapconnect offers G.711 (A-law, µ-law), G.722 and G.729 Called number from To header Works with Kiestoon's registration; switch to Request URI if calls land on the wrong route User agent Kiestoon PBX Cheapconnect reserves the user agent asterisk; Kiestoon already sends its own name

Check the details in your Cheapconnect account

Always use the exact values shown in your own Cheapconnect dashboard: they win over this page.

docs.title: 1. At Cheapconnect
docs.text:
1. Sign in to your Cheapconnect account and open the SIP account (the phone number) you want to use.
  2. Note the SIP username: the number in international format without +, for example 31851234567.
  3. Note the SIP password.
  4. Optional, more secure: limit the account to the public IP address of your Kiestoon server and set a spending limit.

docs.title: 2. In Kiestoon
docs.text:
1. Trunks & routes › Trunks › Add trunk, provider Cheapconnect. The guide is shown in the form as well.
  2. Username: the number, for example 31851234567. Password: the SIP password.
  3. Caller ID: the same Cheapconnect number.
  4. T.38 fax (Advanced): on, if you receive faxes on this number.
  5. Save. The status turns Registered.
  6. Add an inbound route for the number and put the trunk in an outbound route, for example as the second trunk so it takes over when your main provider fails.
  7. Behind NAT? Fill in the public address under Settings → Network and NAT and forward UDP 5060 and the RTP range.

docs.title: If it does not work
docs.text:
Symptom Fix Status Rejected Wrong username or password; copy them again from Cheapconnect Status stays Not registered Check that outgoing UDP 5060 is allowed Incoming calls reach the wrong route Set Called number comes from to Request URI Calls connect but there is no audio NAT: set the public address under Settings and forward the RTP range

Source: Cheapconnect: SIP Trunk Setup, Asterisk & FreePBX.

docs.title: Provider: KPN
docs.text: KPN delivers business SIP trunks (KPN EEN Vast / VoIP Connect) as an IP trunk: there is no registration, KPN recognises your PBX by its fixed public IP address. Kiestoon has a ready-made KPN SIP trunk template.

docs.title: What the template sets
docs.text:
Setting Value Why Authentication IP address KPN only accepts SIP from the PBX addresses on your order Host / port 213.162.171.164, 5060 KPN's standard SBC Provider IP addresses 213.162.171.164, 213.162.171.180 The second SBC is used with Verhoogde Beschikbaarheid (high availability), load-shared Transport TCP KPN supports UDP and TCP and prefers TCP Codecs alaw G.711 A-law (20 ms) is mandatory to the PSTN; G.722/G.729 only work on-net DTMF RFC 2833 / 4733 SIP INFO and KPML are not supported Called number from Request URI KPN sends numbers in international (E.164) notation by default

Your KPN order wins

KPN hands out the SBC addresses and SIP domain per order and can deviate from the standard addresses. The values here come from KPN's configuration guidelines (2017). Always check them against your order.

docs.title: 1. At KPN
docs.text:
1. Give KPN the fixed public IP address of your Kiestoon server when ordering (KTOF form).
  2. Note the SBC address(es) and SIP domain from your order.
  3. Keep the standard profile with numbers in international notation (+31...).

docs.title: 2. In Kiestoon
docs.text:
1. Trunks & routes › Trunks › Add trunk, provider KPN SIP trunk. Change the host and provider IP addresses when your order lists other SBCs.
  2. Caller ID: a number from your KPN block. KPN does not allow other numbers.
  3. T.38 fax (Advanced): on when you receive faxes. KPN offers T.38 first and falls back to G.711.
  4. Save, then add inbound routes for your numbers and an outbound route.
  5. Emergency calls: KPN recognises 112.

docs.title: If it does not work
docs.text:
Symptom Fix No calls at all Check that KPN has the right public IP of this server and that TCP 5060 is open both ways Calls to KPN mobile fail Make sure only alaw is offered Wrong number shown The caller ID must be a number of your KPN trunk; KPN strips P-Asserted-Identity Audio drops on large packets KPN does not allow IP fragmentation; check the MTU on your router

Sources: KPN EEN dienst Vast (VoIP Connect) configuration guidelines, innovaphone: KPN VoIP Connect SIP provider.

docs.title: Provider: Speakup
docs.text: Speakup offers SIP trunks for your own phone system. Kiestoon has a ready-made Speakup template.

docs.title: What the template sets
docs.text:
Setting Value Why Authentication Registration Speakup trunks use a login name and password Host / port sip.speakup.nl, 5060 Speakup's SIP domain; no separate proxy or registrar Transport UDP Codecs alaw,ulaw Speakup supports G.711 A-law, µ-law and G.729 and does no transcoding DTMF RFC 2833 / 4733 Kiestoon's standard Called number from To header Numbers are in 31... format; Kiestoon also matches 0... and +31...

Speakup does not publish a PBX manual

These values come from interop guides by Swyx and Tuxis (a Speakup partner). Always use the details Speakup gives you for your trunk: they win over this page.

docs.title: 1. At Speakup
docs.text:
1. Ask Speakup for the trunk details: login name, password and the numbers of the trunk (31...).
  2. Optional, more secure: ask Speakup to only accept the trunk from the public IP address of your Kiestoon server.

docs.title: 2. In Kiestoon
docs.text:
1. Trunks & routes › Trunks › Add trunk, provider Speakup.
  2. Username: the main number of the trunk, for example 31201234567.
  3. Authentication username: the Speakup login name, when it differs from the number. Password: the trunk password.
  4. Caller ID: one of the trunk numbers. CLIP no screening (showing a number that is not yours) is not allowed in the Netherlands.
  5. T.38 fax: Speakup passes T.38 end to end. For a dedicated fax trunk Speakup uses t38-sbc.speakup.nl: add a second trunk with that host and turn on T.38.
  6. Save, then add inbound routes for the numbers and an outbound route.

docs.title: If it does not work
docs.text:
Symptom Fix Status Rejected Check the login name and password; put the login name in Authentication username Incoming calls reach the wrong route Set Called number comes from to Request URI No audio NAT: check the public address and the RTP port forward

Sources: Swyx: SIP Provider SpeakUp (NL), Tuxis: Speakup trunk instellen.

docs.title: Provider: Voys
docs.text: Kiestoon has a ready-made template for Voys. Voys runs on the VoIPGRID platform and calls a SIP trunk to your own phone system a VoIP trunk.

docs.title: What the template sets
docs.text:
Setting Value Why Authentication Registration Voys gives an Account ID and password per VoIP trunk Host ha.voys.nl Voys' high-availability SIP domain Port 0 (DNS SRV) ha.voys.nl publishes SRV records: UDP 6060 first, 5060 as fallback, on two SIP proxies (Amsterdam and Groningen). Port 0 makes Asterisk follow them, so a failing proxy is skipped Transport UDP Voys supports UDP and TCP; no TLS/SRTP for VoIP trunks Codecs alaw,g722 Voys: preferred codecs G.711 A-law and G.722 Provider IP addresses 195.35.114.0/23, 185.103.76.0/22 Voys sends SIP and media from these ranges. Kiestoon accepts calls from them and opens the firewall for them Called number from Request URI Voys: "Use destination URL from: Request line"; numbers arrive as +31201234567 Caller ID P-Asserted-Identity and Remote-Party-ID Kiestoon sends both; set the CLI header in Freedom to Remote-Party-ID DTMF RFC 4733 Standard

Inbound INVITEs from Voys are not challenged for a password (the "insecure=invite" of old sip.conf guides); they are recognised by source address instead.

docs.title: 1. In Voys Freedom
docs.text:
1. Sign in at freedom.voys.nl and open Admin → VoIP trunks (direct: freedom.voys.nl/redirect/TrunkAccount). Click Add.
  2. Description: for example Kiestoon. Voys also uses it as the outgoing name.
  3. Number of lines: the maximum number of simultaneous calls.
  4. Internal number: a free three-digit number, for example 900.
  5. Call permissions: allow only the destinations you need (for example the Netherlands and Europe). This limits damage if the system is ever misused.
  6. Turn on Use the caller ID of the trunk, so the number Kiestoon sends is shown. Voys only accepts numbers that are assigned to you. With this option on, it overrides "Suppress outgoing number".
  7. Save. Voys generates the Account ID and password. You need both in Kiestoon.
  8. Open Advanced (SIP) settings and set the CLI header to Remote-Party-ID. Leave the static hostname empty: Kiestoon registers itself.
  9. Optional, more secure: under Extra security, allow only the public IP address of your Kiestoon server.
  10. Open the call flow (dial plan) of each Voys number and send incoming calls to this VoIP trunk.

docs.title: 2. In Kiestoon
docs.text:
1. Go to Trunks & routes → Trunks → Add trunk and choose provider Voys. The step-by-step guide is shown in the form as well.
  2. Username: the Account ID. Password: the trunk password. Leave the authentication username empty.
  3. Caller ID: one of your Voys numbers, 0201234567 or +31201234567.
  4. Maximum simultaneous calls: the number of lines from Freedom.
  5. Save. Within a minute the status changes to Registered.
  6. Inbound routes: add a route per Voys number. Voys sends +31201234567; Kiestoon also matches 0201234567 and 31201234567.
  7. Outbound routes: add a route with the Dutch numbers preset and the Voys trunk.
  8. Behind NAT? Fill in the public address under Settings → Network and NAT and forward the SIP port and the RTP range to the server. The Voys ranges are allowed in the Kiestoon firewall automatically.

Anonymous calls: Voys hides your number when you dial 31* before it. Add an outbound pattern with that prefix if you want this.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Status Rejected Wrong Account ID or password. Copy the password again from Freedom Status stays Not registered Your network may block DNS SRV or port 6060. Set host sipproxy.voipgrid.nl and port 5060 Incoming calls reach the wrong route Set Called number comes from to To header One-way or no audio NAT: check the public address and the RTP port forward Wrong number shown Turn on "Use the caller ID of the trunk" in Freedom; the number must be yours

docs.title: Voys terms for your own PBX
docs.text:
• Voys supports connecting a PBX through a VoIP trunk, but does not support configuring the PBX itself.
  • A fraud detection system deactivates a trunk on suspicious traffic. Keep call permissions tight and use the Kiestoon fraud limits.
  • Voys supports every SIP compatible PBX.

Sources: VoIP-trunk: Mijn eigen PBX instellen, Asterisk (Voys help centre), and the DNS SRV records of ha.voys.nl (checked November 2026).

docs.title: Provider: Vodafone Ziggo
docs.text: Vodafone Ziggo Zakelijk delivers SIP trunks with a username and password per trunk. Kiestoon has a ready-made Vodafone Ziggo Zakelijk template.

docs.title: What the template sets
docs.text:
Setting Value Why Authentication Registration Ziggo supplies a username and password; registration every hour Host / port trunk.sipnl.net, 5060 Ziggo's SIP trunk server Transport UDP Codecs alaw,ulaw G.711; check with Ziggo when you want other codecs Called number from To header Numbers are in 31... format; Kiestoon also matches 0... and +31... Fax T.38 Ziggo advises T.38 for fax; turn it on under Advanced

Vodafone Ziggo does not publish a PBX manual

These values come from Panasonic's Ziggo SIP trunk setup guide (2017). Always use the details Ziggo gives you for your trunk: they win over this page.

docs.title: 1. At Vodafone Ziggo
docs.text:
1. Note the username (for example 31123450000, without @trunk.sipnl.net) and the password.
  2. Note the numbers of your number block, also in 31... format.

docs.title: 2. In Kiestoon
docs.text:
1. Trunks & routes › Trunks › Add trunk, provider Vodafone Ziggo Zakelijk.
  2. Username and authentication username: the Ziggo username. Password: the Ziggo password.
  3. Caller ID: a number from your block. Ziggo always adds a P-Asserted-Identity header on incoming calls.
  4. T.38 fax (Advanced): on when you fax.
  5. Save. The status turns Registered. Add inbound routes and an outbound route.
  6. Behind NAT? Fill in the public address under Settings → Network and NAT, forward UDP 5060 and the RTP range, and limit the forward to the Ziggo source addresses.

docs.title: If it does not work
docs.text:
Symptom Fix Status Rejected Check the username (without @trunk.sipnl.net) and the password Incoming calls reach the wrong route Set Called number comes from to Request URI Calls drop behind NAT Check the NAT settings and the port forward

Source: Panasonic: KX-NS setup guide, Ziggo SIP trunk.

docs.title: Kiestoon
docs.text:
De open source telefooncentrale voor het mkb. Eén Debian 13-machine of Proxmox-container draait Asterisk 22 LTS met een modern webportaal: toestellen, bureautelefoons die zichzelf instellen, een visuele keuzemenu-bouwer, wachtrijen, een schakelbord, een gebruikersportaal met doorverbinden door slepen, vestigingen, hoge beschikbaarheid en meer. In het Nederlands en Engels.

Kiestoon installeren Eerste inrichting Wat kan het?

docs.title: Wat kan Kiestoon?
docs.text:
• Telefonie

    Toestellen met voicemail, belgroepen, wachtrijen, vergaderruimtes, tijdcondities met Nederlandse feestdagen, gespreksopname, fax-naar-mail en mail-naar-fax.

    Toestellen

  • Visuele keuzemenu-bouwer

    Sleep stappen op een canvas en trek lijnen ertussen. Elke stap heeft eigen audio: gegenereerd uit tekst, opgenomen in de browser of geüpload. Test het met één klik.

    Keuzemenu (IVR)

  • Telefoons die zichzelf instellen

    Yealink, Snom, Grandstream, Fanvil, Gigaset, Poly, Htek, Akuvox en Cisco. Visuele toetseneditor, uitbreidingsmodules, toetsensjablonen, firmware en zero-touch provisioning.

    Telefoons

  • Receptie en gebruikersportaal

    Een live schakelbord en wallboard, een gebruikersportaal met doorschakelen, voicemail, collega's met beschikbaarheid en doorverbinden door slepen, een browser-softphone en een Windows-softphone.

    Gebruikersportaal

  • Meerdere locaties en hoge beschikbaarheid

    Vestigingen via Kiestoon Edge (zonder port forwarding), gekoppelde Kiestoon-centrales met één telefoonboek, en een actief/passief-paar dat overneemt als een node uitvalt.

    Vestigingen

  • Standaard veilig

    Verplichte MFA voor beheerders, passkeys, SSO (Entra ID, Google, Keycloak, SAML), een beheerde firewall met veilige modus, fail2ban, geoblokkering en bescherming tegen belfraude.

    Beveiliging

  • Back-ups en updates

    Versleutelde volledige en incrementele back-ups naar FTP, FTPS, SFTP, SCP, S3, WebDAV, SMB of OneDrive, herstel vanaf de externe locatie, en updates met één klik op een productie- of testkanaal.

    Back-ups

  • Koppelingen

    Een REST-API met tokens, ondertekende webhooks (inkomend gesprek naar je CRM), een XML- en LDAP-telefoonboek, Prometheus-metrics en een eigen SMTP-server met OAuth2 voor Microsoft 365 en Google.

    API en webhooks

docs.title: Waar begin je?
docs.text:
1. Installeer Kiestoon in een Proxmox-container of op een Debian 13-machine.
  2. Volg de eerste inrichting: beheerder, nummerplan, trunk, toestellen en telefoons.
  3. Lees hoe Kiestoon werkt voor de ideeën achter bestemmingen, rollen en het nummerplan.

Hulp vanuit het portaal

Elke pagina in het Kiestoon-portaal heeft bovenaan een knop Help. Die opent de bijbehorende pagina van deze handleiding, in de taal waarin je het portaal gebruikt.

docs.title: AI-samenvattingen
docs.text: Kiestoon kan opgenomen gesprekken en voicemailberichten uitschrijven en samenvatten: waar het gesprek over ging, wat er is afgesproken en welke actiepunten er liggen. Open AI in het menu Systeem.

docs.title: Zo werkt het
docs.text:
1. De transcriptie wordt altijd op de server gemaakt door Whisper (zie Spraak). Audio verlaat de telefooncentrale nooit.
  2. De samenvatting komt van de engine die u kiest:
Engine Wat het betekent Lokaal model (standaard) Een taalmodel draait op de server zelf met llama.cpp. Gratis en privé: er verlaat niets de server. Het is trager en heeft vrij geheugen nodig (ongeveer 4 GB voor Qwen3 4B, 2 GB voor Qwen3 1.7B). Het model start zodra er werk is en stopt na 5 minuten zonder werk Claude (cloud) Snellere en betere samenvattingen van Claude van Anthropic, met uw eigen API-sleutel (aan te maken op console.anthropic.com). Alleen de tekst van de transcriptie wordt verstuurd; Anthropic rekent het gebruik af met uw account

De API-sleutel wordt los van de andere instellingen bewaard en na opslaan nooit meer getoond (u ziet alleen de laatste vier tekens). Verwijder hem met Sleutel verwijderen.

docs.title: Wat samenvatten
docs.text:
Instelling Wat het doet Opgenomen gesprekken Nieuwe opnames (van gesprekken die toch al worden opgenomen) worden op de achtergrond uitgeschreven en samengevat, nieuwste eerst, één tegelijk Voicemail Voicemailberichten krijgen een samenvatting en actiepunten in het gebruikersportaal, de Windows-softphone en de voicemailmail Taal van de samenvattingen Zelfde als het gesprek, of altijd Nederlands of Engels Samenvattingen van gesprekken bewaren Verwijdert samenvattingen en transcripties van gesprekken na dit aantal dagen. 0 bewaart ze zolang de opname bestaat

Druk op Uitproberen om een voorbeeldvoicemail samen te vatten met de huidige instellingen, nog voor u ze opslaat.

docs.title: Samenvattingen bij opnames
docs.text:
Onder Opnames (en Mijn gesprekken in het portaal) toont een gesprek met een samenvatting het onderwerp en de stemming van de beller. Klik op de sterretjesknop voor de samenvatting, de actiepunten en de volledige transcriptie. Receptie en beheerders kunnen een losse opname ook direct Uitschrijven en samenvatten, ook als automatische samenvattingen uit staan.

Spraakherkenning kan fouten maken

Een samenvatting is zo goed als de transcriptie. Controleer namen en nummers met de opname. Het model krijgt de opdracht niets te verzinnen dat niet in de transcriptie staat.

docs.title: Vereisten
docs.text:
• Het pakket kiestoon-speech (versie 1.1.0 of nieuwer bevat llama.cpp voor het lokale model).
  • Spraak-naar-tekst aan onder Spraak, met een gedownload Whisper-model.
  • Voor het lokale model: het model gedownload op de AI-pagina (vaste SHA-256-controlesommen).

docs.title: API, webhooks en metrics
docs.text: Alles wat het webportaal doet, gaat via dezelfde JSON-API onder /api/. Andere programma's (een CRM, een helpdesk, scripts) gebruiken die met een API-token. Webhooks laten die programma's weten wanneer er iets gebeurt.

docs.title: API-tokens
docs.text:
Maak een token aan onder Integraties › API-tokens › Nieuw token. Het token wordt één keer getoond; Kiestoon bewaart alleen een hash ervan.

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer kt_…" https://pbx.example.com/api/pbx/extensions
  • Een token heeft een rol (admin, reception of user) en nooit meer rechten dan de gebruiker die het maakte op dat moment heeft. Een token van een uitgeschakelde gebruiker werkt niet meer.
  • Een alleen-lezen-token kan alleen GET gebruiken.
  • Tokens kunnen niet bij /api/tokens, /api/webhooks, /api/users, /api/account, /api/auth, /api/system/updates of /api/backups/restore.
  • Schrijfverzoeken sturen JSON met Content-Type: application/json.
  • Fouten komen terug als {"error": "<code>", "field": "<veld>"} met een 4xx- of 5xx-status.

docs.title: Handige endpoints
docs.text: Methode Pad Rol Wat GET /api/pbx/extensions admin Alle toestellen GET /api/live reception Lopende gesprekken, status van trunks GET /api/reception/queues reception Wachtrijen met wachtende bellers en medewerkers GET /api/cdr reception Gespreksgeschiedenis (call detail records); /api/cdr/export geeft CSV GET /api/phonebook user Het centrale telefoonboek POST /api/phonebook reception Contact toevoegen {name, company, work, mobile, other, email, notes} POST /api/calls reception Click-to-call {extension: "201", number: "0201234567"}: eerst gaat het toestel over GET /api/faxes reception Ontvangen faxen; GET /api/faxes/{id}/pdf downloadt er een POST /api/fax/send reception Fax versturen {boxId, number, name, pdf}; pdf is de PDF in base64 (maximaal ongeveer 11 MB) GET /api/fax/jobs reception Uitgaande faxen met hun status (queued, sending, success, failed)

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
Voeg een webhook toe onder Integrations › Webhooks › Webhook toevoegen en kies de gebeurtenissen. Kiestoon stuurt een POST met JSON naar je URL:

{
  "id": "4f1c2a…",
  "event": "call.ringing",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-15T09:30:12Z",
  "data": { "callId": "1731663012.42", "from": "0612345678", "fromName": "", "did": "0201234567", "extension": "201", "direction": "inbound" }
}
Gebeurtenis Wanneer Data call.ringing Een inkomend gesprek gaat over op een toestel callId, from, fromName, did, extension, direction call.answered Een inkomend gesprek wordt aangenomen hetzelfde als call.ringing call.ended Een gesprek is afgelopen het call detail record voicemail.updated Het aantal berichten van een voicemailbox veranderde mailbox, new, old fax.received Er kwam een fax binnen id, box, status, pages, caller, did queue.abandoned Een beller hing op terwijl hij in een wachtrij wachtte queue, from, fromName, position, holdTime, callId

docs.title: Headers en handtekening
Telefoonboek voor telefoons
docs.text:
• XML-telefoonboeken: /prov/phonebook/{yealink|snom|fanvil}.xml en /prov/phonebook/grandstream/phonebook.xml, achter de gebruikersnaam en het wachtwoord van provisioning. Geprovisionede telefoons krijgen het adres automatisch.
  • LDAP: base DN ou=phonebook,dc=kiestoon, attributen cn, sn, givenName, o, telephoneNumber, mobile, homePhone, mail. Bind als cn=<provisioning-gebruiker>,ou=phonebook,dc=kiestoon met het provisioning-wachtwoord als "Wachtwoord verplicht" aan staat. Alleen bereikbaar vanaf de netwerken die SIP mogen gebruiken.

docs.title: Prometheus-metrics
docs.text:
Zet Internettoegang › Prometheus-metrics › Metrics publiceren aan. Kiestoon levert dan GET /metrics (buiten /api/) in het tekstformaat van Prometheus. Prometheus stuurt het token als bearer-token; adressen in de lijst "Toegestaan zonder token" mogen zonder token ophalen.

- job_name: kiestoon
  scheme: https
  authorization:
    credentials: <token>
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['pbx.example.com']
Metric Wat kiestoon_info{version} Altijd 1, met de draaiende versie kiestoon_uptime_seconds Seconden sinds het portaal startte kiestoon_asterisk_connected 1 als het portaal met Asterisk praat kiestoon_active_calls, kiestoon_active_calls_by_direction{direction} Lopende gesprekken kiestoon_calls_today Gesprekken sinds middernacht kiestoon_extensions, kiestoon_registered_endpoints Toestellen en geregistreerde telefoons kiestoon_trunk_up{trunk} 1 als een trunk geregistreerd of bereikbaar is kiestoon_queue_waiting_callers{queue}, kiestoon_queue_longest_wait_seconds{queue}, kiestoon_queue_available_agents{queue} Status van wachtrijen kiestoon_queue_completed_total{queue}, kiestoon_queue_abandoned_total{queue} Tellers van wachtrijen sinds de laatste herstart van Asterisk kiestoon_fax_jobs{status} Uitgaande faxen per status kiestoon_mail_queue_length Mails die wachten op verzending kiestoon_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{target} Laatste geslaagde back-up per locatie

docs.title: Privacybeleid van de Kiestoon-app
docs.text:
Geldt voor de Kiestoon-app voor Android en iPhone, uitgegeven door RHIS. Laatst bijgewerkt: 27 november 2026.

De Kiestoon-app is de mobiele client van een Kiestoon-telefooncentrale. Die centrale wordt beheerd door je werkgever of hun IT-partner (de "organisatie"), niet door RHIS. De app maakt rechtstreeks verbinding met de centrale van je organisatie; RHIS beheert die centrale niet en kan je gesprekken, contacten, gespreksgeschiedenis en voicemail niet zien.

docs.title: Wat de app verwerkt, en waar het naartoe gaat
docs.text:
Gegevens Waarom Waar het naartoe gaat Adres van de telefooncentrale en de inlogsessie Om verbinding te maken met je centrale Alleen opgeslagen op je telefoon Microfoongeluid tijdens een gesprek Om te kunnen bellen Rechtstreeks naar de centrale van je organisatie, versleuteld (DTLS-SRTP). Nooit naar RHIS. De microfoon wordt alleen tijdens een gesprek gebruikt Pushtoken van je telefoon (van Google Firebase Cloud Messaging of Apple) en de naam van de telefoon (bijvoorbeeld "Pixel 9") Om de app te laten overgaan als hij dicht is, en om de telefoon te tonen onder Mijn apparaten Naar de centrale van je organisatie. Het pushtoken wordt verzegeld door de pushdienst van RHIS, zie hieronder Je collega's, telefoonboek, gespreksgeschiedenis, wachtrijen en voicemail Om ze in de app te tonen Opgehaald van de centrale van je organisatie en getoond in de app. Niet opgeslagen door RHIS

De centrale van je organisatie houdt eigen gegevens bij (bijvoorbeeld de gespreksgeschiedenis). Daarvoor is je organisatie verantwoordelijk; vraag hen om hun privacybeleid.

docs.title: De pushdienst van RHIS
docs.text:
Google en Apple bezorgen meldingen voor een app alleen namens de uitgever, dus de centrale van je organisatie stuurt wekmeldingen via de pushdienst van RHIS (push.rhis.nl):

  • Hij bewaart niets: het pushtoken wordt omgezet in een verzegelde sleutel die alleen de pushdienst kan openen, en die sleutel wordt bewaard door de centrale van je organisatie, niet door RHIS.
